Title: Mi Technovation buys Singapore building for RM332mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mi Technovation Bhd is buying a seven-storey industrial building in Singapore for RM331.8 million to establish a global operational hub for its vehicle technologies business.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the proposed acquisition would support the expansion of its vehicle technologies business unit (VTBU).
VTBU is developing and commercialising electric powertrain systems and related core components.
Mi Technovation said its subsidiary Ohima International Pte Ltd signed a conditional sale and purchase agreement with Kim Hup Lee & Co (Private) Ltd to buy the KHL Building at 25 New Industrial Road.
The purchase consideration is based on an independent valuation of the property as at Sept 17.
The vacant freehold property has a gross floor area of 10,348.4 square metres, or about 111,389 square feet, and is located near the Tai Seng and Paya Lebar precincts, about 9.3km from Singapore's city centre.
Mi Technovation said the property would serve as VTBU's future Singapore headquarters and global operational hub.
"The property is expected to house a main data and computing centre, a digital twin and artificial intelligence centre, a product definition and strategy centre, a worldwide sales and marketing centre, a worldwide finance and legal centre, a customer experience centre and other ancillary facilities," it said,
The company said VTBU's progress in developing and commercialising its electric powertrain systems, alongside revenue generation in the first half of the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026, had created the need for a larger facility.
Currently, VTBU operates rented manufacturing and research and development facilities in Hangzhou, Xi'an and Chongqing, China, with a combined built-up area of about 10,809 sq m.
Its existing Singapore headquarters occupies a leased 568 sq m building in Queenstown.
The lease runs until Nov 30, 2028, after which the company intends to relocate its headquarters to KHL Building.
The acquisition is expected to generate annual rental savings of about S$330,000 (RM1.05 million).
Mi Technovation said ownership of the property would provide it with greater control and flexibility over its operational premises, while reducing reliance on leased facilities and uncertainty over rental costs.
The purchase will be funded through a combination of bank borrowings, proceeds from the listing of Mi Material Holding Ltd on the Singapore Exchange and internally generated funds.
The indicative funding comprises S$77.4 million in bank borrowings, S$25.44 million from the listing proceeds and S$1.04 million in internal funds.
The company also expects to incur about S$5.31 million in incidental acquisition costs.
The acquisition is subject to shareholders' approval at an extraordinary general meeting and other relevant approvals.

Title: NSTP booth draws crowds at Jom Heboh with 600 free newspapers daily
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Crowds have flocked to The New Straits Times Press (Malaysia) Bhd (NSTP) booth at Karnival Jom Heboh (KJH) Johor Baru 2026, attracted by its daily distribution of 600 free newspapers and a range of interactive activities.
The initiative aims to promote print media while adding to the carnival's attractions through activities supported by sponsors Nestle, Nibou and Yakult.
NSTP Branding and Intellectual Property Department head Tengku Kaifimirza Tuan Cherit @ Tengku Hamzah said the sponsors' participation reflected their continued commitment to supporting NSTP's community-based programmes.
"We are grateful for the strong support from sponsors such as Nestle, Nibou and Yakult at the NSTP booth this time.
"Such strategic partnerships not only enliven the carnival but also add value for visitors, who can enjoy quality food and beverages from the sponsors," he said.
Also present was NSTP Branding and Intellectual Property Department senior officer Wan Fazly Hizam Wan Kadir.
Tengku Kaifimirza said the booth's main attractions included a colouring and drawing competition for children aged below 12, with prizes worth RM150.
The prize-giving ceremony is scheduled for Sunday.
"Registration is open daily at RM10 per entry. Each participant will receive attractive products from our sponsors," he said.
KJH Johor Baru 2026 features various attractions, including sales booths, performances by local artistes, family activities and promotions on everyday essentials.
Recognised by the Malaysia Book of Records (MBOR) as the 'Longest Running Outdoor Carnival', KJH is being held over 3 days until Sunday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police open two investigation papers after Kluang LED screens hacked to show obscene videos
Article:
KLUANG: Police have opened two investigation papers following reports that eight light-emitting diode (LED) screens installed around the town were hacked and used to display obscene videos yesterday.
Kluang police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh said police received a report from a 42-year-old man today.
"The report was related, among other things, to the LED screen system displaying obscene content.
"Initial investigations found that the complainant was informed by his staff that eight screens installed around Kluang was hacked yesterday.
"The complainant received several messages via WhatsApp containing screenshots and videos of the obscene content displayed on the LED screens.
"Following the incident, the complainant contacted the supplier for confirmation before taking steps to cut off the power supply to stop the display," he said in a statement.
Bahrin said police were investigating the case under Section 4(1) of the Computer Crimes Act and Section 292 of the Penal Code.
"Those with information about the incident are urged to contact any nearby police station to assist in the investigation," he said.
Earlier, the Kluang Municipal Council (MPK)
confirmed
that its LED display system had been hacked. The council apologised for the inconvenience.
Yesterday, images and videos of several LED screens installed by MPK displaying obscene content went viral on social media and WhatsApp groups.

Title: AAPA: Asia Pacific airlines carry 30.4mil international passengers in September
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Asia Pacific airlines carried 30.4 million international passengers in September 2026, up 0.7 per cent from a year earlier.
Air cargo demand grew 6.4 per cent, according to preliminary figures from the Association of Asia Pacific Airlines (AAPA).
AAPA director general Wong Hong said passenger numbers increased following five consecutive months of year-on-year declines with stronger growth in longer-haul travel and international air cargo demand.
"September saw passenger numbers increase slightly compared to a year earlier with stronger growth in longer-haul travel, while air cargo demand gained momentum," he said in a statement.
AAPA said passenger traffic remained uneven across markets with capacity reductions contributing to lower passenger numbers on some routes.
However, longer-haul markets continued to grow, partly supported by passengers choosing routes that avoided Middle East hubs.
International passenger demand, measured in revenue passenger kilometres (RPK), increased 5.9 per cent year-on-year, while available seat capacity expanded 6.8 per cent.
AAPA said this resulted in a 0.6 percentage point decline in the average international passenger load factor to 80.2 per cent.
On air cargo, AAPA said stronger global manufacturing activity, increased purchases of raw materials and components, and sustained demand for artificial intelligence (AI)-related goods supported growth.
International air cargo demand, measured in freight tonne kilometres (FTK), rose 6.4 per cent year-on-year, exceeding the 4.9 per cent increase in available freight capacity.
The average international freight load factor increased 0.8 percentage points to 60.3 per cent.
For the first nine months of 2026, Asia Pacific airlines carried 289.5 million international passengers, up 1.9 per cent from the corresponding period last year.
International passenger demand, measured in RPK, rose 4.6 per cent during the period, while air cargo demand increased 5.6 per cent.
Wong said passenger markets continued to adjust to changes in capacity and travel patterns, while stronger manufacturing activity and demand for AI-related goods supported cargo traffic.
He said elevated jet fuel prices, airspace restrictions and weaker Asian currencies continued to put pressure on airlines' operating costs and profitability.
Wong said year-end holiday travel should support passenger demand, while continued investment in AI infrastructure and related trade flows was expected to benefit air cargo markets.
However, he said higher travel and shipping costs could affect growth, while geopolitical tensions and changes in trade policies remained key uncertainties.
AAPA's member airlines include Malaysia Airlines Bhd, Air Astana, Air India, Air New Zealand, All Nippon Airways, Bangkok Airways, Cathay Pacific, China Airlines, EVA Airways, Garuda Indonesia, Japan Airlines, Lion Air, Philippine Airlines, Qantas Airways, Royal Brunei Airlines, Singapore Airlines, Thai Airways International and Vietnam Airlines.

Title: UEM Sunrise, AME Elite team up for RM4bil industrial park
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: UEM Sunrise Bhd and AME Elite Consortium Bhd have formed a 50:50 joint venture to develop a 162.7-hectare industrial park in Gerbang Nusajaya, with a gross development value (GDV) of RM4 billion.
In a joint statement, the companies said the project will be developed in three phases.
The first phase is expected to begin by the end of 2027.
The joint venture company Gerbang Synergy Sdn Bhd will buy the freehold land from UEM Sunrise's unit Nusajaya Rise Sdn Bhd for RM972.1 million.
The partnership combines UEM Sunrise's landbank and township planning capabilities with AME Elite's industrial park development expertise and multinational client network.
UEM Sunrise managing director and chief executive officer Shaharul Farez Hassan said the collaboration would accelerate the development of Gerbang Nusajaya while allowing both companies to share investment and execution risks.
"The joint venture also reflects our disciplined approach to capital allocation and portfolio optimisation.
"It enables us to share development investment and execution risks with an experienced partner, while retaining meaningful participation in the long-term value creation of the development.
"With the momentum surrounding Johor and the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), we believe Gerbang Nusajaya is well positioned to play an increasingly important role in Iskandar Puteri's next phase of growth," he said.
AME Elite executive director and group chief executive officer Dylan Tan Teck Eng said the project would expand the company's industrial development pipeline and strengthen its presence in Iskandar Puteri.
He said demand for integrated, environmentally sustainable industrial facilities was growing as companies expanded their operations within the JS-SEZ.
"This project will equip global and domestic players with high-specification facilities, continuing to set the benchmark for industrial real estate," he said.
The proposed industrial park will target foreign and domestic investors in high-value sectors, including electrical and electronics (E&E), medical devices and advanced logistics.
Its development comes amid growing investment activity in Johor, which secured RM110 billion in approved investments in 2025, including RM77 billion from the JS-SEZ.
The economic zone aims to attract 100 investment projects and create 20,000 skilled jobs over its first decade.
Located about 15 minutes from the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link and Sultan Abu Bakar Customs, Immigration and Quarantine Complex, the industrial park will offer cross-border connectivity to Singapore.
It will also have access to the Second Link Expressway, KTM railway network, Port of Tanjung Pelepas and Senai International Airport, supporting manufacturers and logistics operators.

Title: Anwar directs agencies to address e-commerce complaints from consumers, traders
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed agencies to take immediate action to address complaints from consumers and traders over various issues involving e-commerce platforms.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the directive had been issued to the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry and the Communications Ministry, particularly the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).
"The prime minister raised concerns over problems faced by users of e-commerce platforms, particularly the high commission fees imposed on sellers and instances where products received did not match what had been ordered.
"He has asked the relevant ministries and agencies to take action on several issues, particularly fraud and scams on e-commerce platforms," he said at a post-cabinet press conference.
Fahmi said MCMC had recently held a meeting with all major e-commerce platform operators to discuss the issues.
He added that a coordination retreat involving enforcement agencies would also be held within the next few weeks to develop a coordinated approach to addressing problems faced by e-commerce platform users.
"Tomorrow, during the National Courier Day celebration, I will make several additional announcements relating to this issue."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Roblox taps Malaysia's Joel Neoh to lead Southeast Asia, Oceania
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Roblox has appointed Malaysian entrepreneur Joel Neoh as managing director for Southeast Asia and Oceania as the global gaming and creation platform looks to expand its presence in the regions.
Neoh, who joined the company in October, will lead Roblox's regional business strategy, foster partnerships, support the creator ecosystem and align global product and business priorities with local market demands.
His responsibilities include strengthening the regional creator ecosystem, supporting local developers and studios in scaling their businesses and raising awareness of the Roblox brand among players and parents.
Roblox said Southeast Asia and Oceania offer significant long-term growth opportunities, supported by their young, digitally savvy populations and rapidly evolving digital ecosystems.
Neoh said the region's creativity, optimism and entrepreneurial energy present opportunities to help more people move from consuming digital content to creating their own experiences.
"We have an opportunity to help a new generation of creators across Southeast Asia and Oceania turn ideas into experiences, communities and businesses that can reach the world.
"As we grow, keeping young people safe and working closely with parents, regulators and local communities will remain central to everything we do.
"I believe this region can become one of the most important sources of creativity on Roblox, helping reimagine the way people come together through play and creation," he said in a statement.
Roblox vice president of international Zhen Fang said Southeast Asia and Oceania are important markets for the company in Asia Pacific, with growing communities of creators and players.
He said Neoh's two decades of experience building businesses across the region, coupled with his connections to the local technology ecosystem, make him suitable to lead Roblox's next phase of growth.
Neoh brings two decades of experience founding and scaling technology businesses across Asia Pacific, covering digital media, e-commerce, financial technology, consumer health and artificial intelligence.
He founded Malaysian e-commerce platform GroupsMore, which merged with Groupon ahead of the latter's initial public offering, before taking on a leadership role at Groupon Asia Pacific.
He subsequently founded Fave, a Southeast Asian fintech and consumer payments platform that grew to more than 10 million users before being acquired by Pine Labs in 2021.
Most recently, Neoh served as managing director at Prenetics, where he led its consumer health businesses.
He is also an active investor who has backed more than 50 start-ups across Asia, particularly in consumer technology.
Neoh is a founding partner of First Move, an early-stage venture capital platform supporting entrepreneurs in Southeast Asia.
He was also involved in the launch of IM8.

Title: Nestlé, Red Crescent ready 7,000 flood aid packs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Nestlé Malaysia and the Malaysian Red Crescent (MRC) have prepared 7,000 flood aid packs worth about RM1.8 million to support families in flood-prone communities as the monsoon season approaches.
The relief supplies are already being sent to Kedah, Kelantan, Pahang and Terengganu.
A separate initiative in Sabah has mobilised 40 volunteers to prepare 1,000 aid bags for deployment within the state.
The annual Nationwide Flood Aid Relief initiative marks the fourth consecutive year of collaboration between Nestlé Malaysia and MRC.
Since 2023, the partnership has provided assistance to more than 30,000 families affected by floods and strengthened MRC's emergency response capabilities, including funding for a new ambulance.
Nestlé Malaysia chief executive officer Juan Aranols said advance preparation was crucial to ensuring essential food and beverage supplies could reach affected communities quickly when disasters struck.
He said the collaboration leveraged MRC's humanitarian network and the commitment of volunteers to improve flood preparedness nationwide.
The aid packs contain essential food and beverage products, including Milo, Nescafe, Milo, Maggi, Nestlé breakfast cereals, Nestim, Lactogroe and Everyday.
The Kuala Lumpur packing exercise involved Nestlé Malaysia employees, MRC volunteers and representatives from Universiti Malaya, Universiti Malaya-Wales and Yayasan Wakaf.
In Sabah, employees from Nestlé's local operations, Harrisons Sabah and MRC Sabah worked together to prepare the additional aid bags.
MRC national chairperson Tan Sri Tunku Puteri Intan Safinaz Sultan Abdul Halim Mu'adzam Shah said preparing supplies before floods occurred would enable humanitarian assistance to be deployed more effectively.
The initiative also involves the National Disaster Management Agency and its agencies as partners in this year's relief efforts.
The programme forms part of Nestlé Sayang Komuniti, which mobilises employees for community and humanitarian causes.
Separately, Nestlé Malaysia collaborated with Yayasan Food Bank Malaysia to prepare 800 food and nutrition aid packs for families in remote areas of Tumpat and Jeli, Kelantan, ahead of the monsoon season.
A total of 400 employees participated in this year's relief initiatives.

Title: Mahadev Shankar: A life devoted to justice, integrity and public service
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than two decades ago, the late former Court of Appeal judge Datuk Mahadev Shankar wrote that death would be meaningless if it did not put life into perspective.
Today, those words carry deeper significance as the legal fraternity mourns a man who devoted more than six decades of his life to the pursuit of justice and public service.
Mahadev, one of the country's most respected legal minds, died on Monday at the age of 94.
In a tribute today, Malaysian Bar president Anand Raj described Mahadev as a towering figure whose contributions extended far beyond the courtroom.
"While we mourn his passing, we must celebrate his life.
"For those of us who have dedicated our lives to the law, we can pay no greater compliment than to say that his was a life to emulate," he said in a statement.
Anand said Mahadev was widely respected for his sharp judicial mind, mastery of languages and unwavering commitment to justice.
He recalled how Mahadev had criticised delays in the judicial system, warning that litigants often obtained judgments so late that their victories became meaningless.
"Too many litigants get their awards so many years later that victory is academic or worse still pyrrhic!
"This is not something we should encourage," Mahadev had said in a 1998 judgment.
Anand said Mahadev was equally firm on professional ethics, having warned that lawyers found stealing money from their clients' accounts should be struck off the Rolls.
A former Victoria Institution student, Mahadev was called to the Bar of the Inner Temple in England in 1955.
He was admitted as an advocate and solicitor of the High Court of Malaya in August 1956 and began his legal career at Shearn Delamore & Co, where he became a partner at 29.
He also served as an elected Bar Council member for several terms between 1965 and 1973.
In 1979, Mahadev was among 13 lawyers appointed as judicial commissioners to help clear the High Court's backlog of cases.
He became a High Court judge in 1983 before being appointed to the newly established Court of Appeal in 1994, where he served until his retirement in 1997.
Beyond the Bench, Mahadev served on three Royal Commissions of Inquiry, including those investigating injuries sustained by Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in 1999 and the controversial V.K. Lingam video clip in 2007.
He was also among the founding commissioners of the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam), serving from 2000 to 2002.
In 2014, the Malaysian Bar conferred on him its Lifetime Achievement Award in recognition of his contributions to the legal profession.
Anand also recalled Mahadev's views on the importance of maintaining public confidence in the judiciary.
"The judiciary must have the confidence of the community.
"It is not just a question of actual bias. It is also the perception of bias," Mahadev had said in a 2014 interview.
Anand said Mahadev had earned and commanded the confidence of the legal community until the end of his life.
He also extended the Malaysian Bar's condolences to Mahadev's wife, Datin Janet Kuek, their children and family members.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCA gets fourth seat as BN takes Kota Laksamana from PN
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MCA will contest four seats in the Melaka election after securing Kota Laksamana, a constituency initially allocated to Perikatan Nasional (PN).
The latest allocation brings Barisan Nasional's (BN) total to 23 seats, leaving PN and its allies with five of the 28 state constituencies.
MCA announced the additional seat in a Facebook post today, naming Melvin Chua Kew Wei as its candidate for Kota Laksamana.
"To voters in Melaka, these are the best candidates to represent you in the state assembly. Vote for BN candidates," the post read.
Kota Laksamana had previously been allocated to PN as its sixth seat, with the coalition announcing on Thursday that its candidate would be named later.
PN had unveiled five candidates, comprising two each from Pas and Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan), and one from Gerakan.
They included Hang Tuah Jaya Pas committee member Ridzuan Sarif, who will contest Bukit Katil, and Tangga Batu Pas deputy chief Rafie Ahmad, who will contest Paya Rumput.
However, Kota Laksamana was subsequently allocated to MCA, reducing PN's share to five seats.
MCA will also field incumbents Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem in Machap Jaya and Datuk Lim Ban Hong in Klebang, while Melaka Historic City Council member Jasmine Lok Huey Yee will contest Bandar Hilir.
The party's allocation has increased twice since BN announced its candidates on Oct 24, when MCA was initially allocated just two seats.
It subsequently secured Bandar Hilir before adding Kota Laksamana, bringing its total to four seats, compared with 7 in the 2021 election.
MCA will defend Machap Jaya and Klebang, its only victories in the 2021 election, while attempting to wrest Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir from DAP.
The Election Commission has fixed nomination day for Oct 31, with polling scheduled for Nov 14.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah rural road projects must proceed, says Ewon
Article:
PENAMPANG: The 13 rural road projects in Sabah whose Letters of Acceptance (LOA) have been deferred must still be implemented, said Penampang member of parliament Datuk Ewon Benedick.
He said clarification was needed on the status of the projects, including whether they had been cancelled or postponed to the following year.
"As far as I am concerned, MPs and the people of Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia need further clarification.
"As the Penampang MP, I want an explanation on the status of the 13 projects whose LOA have been deferred. What is the current status of these roads?
"I have asked whether they have been cancelled or carried forward to the following year for implementation, but there has been no clarification so far," he said after inspecting the Terian and Buayan road upgrade projects here.
On Monday, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is also rural and regional development minister, told the Dewan Rakyat that projects in Sabah and Sarawak had been cancelled despite funds having been allocated for them.
Ewon, who is also Sabah Deputy Chief Minister III and Industrial Development, Entrepreneurship and Transport Minister, said the projects should not be sidelined as they had been planned and repeatedly proposed by various parties.
This includes proposal from the State Economic Planning Unit, Public Works Department and elected representatives.
"We cannot sideline the rights of people who have been waiting for rural road facilities.
"We want projects that have been agreed upon and approved to proceed.
"If they cannot be implemented this year due to allocation constraints, there should be room to give them priority for implementation next year."

Title: Coffee shop association urges crackdown on illicit cigarettes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Singapore Coffee Shop Proprietors' General Association (MSCSPGA) has called for stricter and more frequent enforcement against retailers selling illicit cigarettes.
It warned that the widespread trade is putting legitimate coffee shop operators at a competitive disadvantage.
The association said illicit cigarettes remained easily accessible in many neighbourhoods, with sales allegedly involving foreign workers operating retail outlets.
Citing a Wawasanex survey conducted in May, MSCSPGA said 68.8 per cent of illicit cigarette buyers identified migrant workers as the main sellers, while 99 per cent said illicit cigarettes were easy or very easy to obtain.
"Our members see it every day. Customers finish their coffee in our outlets and buy cheap cigarettes just a few doors away, often from a foreign worker behind the counter.
"We run our businesses by the rules and pay our taxes, but we simply cannot compete with those prices," president Wong Teu Hoon said in a statement.
The association welcomed Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh's directive for Kuala Lumpur City Hall to revoke and blacklist business licences held by Malaysians who sublet their premises to foreigners.
It urged local councils nationwide to adopt similar measures against outlets found selling illicit cigarettes.
MSCSPGA also cited recent enforcement operations in Kuala Selangor, where three premises were ordered to close and 18 compounds were issued during a joint operation involving the Kuala Selangor Municipal Council, Customs Department and Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry.
The association also welcomed the government's RM1.1 billion allocation under the 2027 Budget to strengthen enforcement agencies.
It said the funds should support more frequent inspections, business licence checks and tougher action against repeat offenders.
The association said there is a need for sustained enforcement rather than one-off raids, with follow-up inspections to ensure outlets caught violating the law do not reopen under different names or licences.
"That is how honest coffeeshop operators can compete on fair terms," it said.
Established in 1947, MSCSPGA represents 20,000 members through 44 affiliates across Malaysia and Singapore.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM5bil China loan redirected to Perak water project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has repurposed RM5 billion of loans from China to finance a major water supply project in Perak, turning part of the financial liability from two abandoned pipeline projects into funding for essential infrastructure.
The RM5 billion, originally linked to the Trans-Sabah gas pipeline (TSGP) and multi-product pipeline (MPP) projects which were terminated in 2018, was redirected towards the northern Perak water supply scheme (NPWSS).
Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim witnessed the signing of an agreement between Suria Strategic Energy Resources Sdn Bhd, a Finance Ministry-owned company, and the Export-Import Bank of China (Cexim) on Thursday.
The Finance Ministry said the move converts part of the financial liability arising from two abandoned pipeline projects into funding for essential water infrastructure.
Following the cancellation of the TSGP and MPP projects, Malaysia remained liable for RM8 billion in loans from Cexim despite the pipelines never being completed.
The government said the agreement marked a partial recovery of the financial losses arising from the abandoned projects, following negotiations with the Chinese bank.
The ministry said the previous three administrations had been unable to resolve the outstanding loan issue despite efforts to do so.
The agreement marks a significant achievement for the Madani government in concluding negotiations and achieving a partial recovery on the loan by repurposing RM5 billion to implement NPWSS, it added.
"Thus, reducing the losses arising from the TSGP and MPP projects and ensuring that RM5 billion can be utilised to develop essential infrastructure that benefits the rakyat, particularly in the states of Perak and Penang," it said.
The NPWSS will involve transferring raw water from Sungai Perak to Bukit Merah Dam, upgrading infrastructure along Sungai Kurau and Terusan Besar, and building water treatment plants in Kamunting and Bogak.
Once completed, the scheme is targeted to supply up to 700 million litres of treated water daily to northern Perak, including the Kerian industrial area, and 300 million litres daily to Penang.
It will also provide 500 million litres of raw water daily for agricultural irrigation.
The project is expected to strengthen water security, meet rising demand from households, industries and farms, and support economic development in northern Perak and Penang.
"Water security is among the government's priorities to ensure the well-being of the people and strengthen economic development, especially in the northern Perak region.
"The implementation of NPWSS is expected to strengthen long-term water security, meet the increasing demand for domestic, agricultural, and industrial uses and support socioeconomic development," the ministry said.
Construction works will be undertaken by local contractors, providing opportunities for domestic companies to participate in the infrastructure project.
The signing was also witnessed by Deputy Prime Minister and Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Cexim chairman Chen Huaiyu and representatives of the Chinese embassy and China National Petroleum Corporation.
The agreement was signed by SSER board member Mohd Fariszan Ahmad and Cexim vice-president Kang Wang.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Penang Budget: RM500 aid for newlyweds among new state initiatives
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Newlyweds in Penang will receive a one-off RM500 cash incentive next year under a new initiative aimed at expanding the state's social safety net.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow announced the initiative, known as the "Mempelai Emas" programme, when tabling the 2027 Budget at the state legislative assembly.
"In 2027, alongside maintaining our allocation commitment of RM58 million, the state government will expand the i-Sejahtera Programme through the introduction of the Mempelai Emas programme, as a token of appreciation to couples newly tying the knot in Penang.
"Couples who meet the eligibility criteria will receive a one-off contribution of RM500," he said.
The marriage incentive is among several new welfare measures and initiatives announced for next year.
To support gig-economy workers, Chow announced a one-off RM600 incentive for eligible e-hailing drivers, with an allocation ceiling of RM9 million.
For the first time, the state will also establish the Penang State Social Development Fund (Tabung Pembangunan Sosial Negeri Pulau Pinang), with an initial allocation of RM350,000.
"The fund is designed to roll out targeted welfare drives, tackle poverty, and curb social disparity among marginalised groups," he said.
Addressing changing household demographics, Chow said the Penang State Housing Board would begin studying co-living residential concepts in selected government rental and People's Housing Programme (PPR) units to cater to single individuals and elderly residents living alone.
"By introducing a shared or communal living model within existing or repurposed public housing inventory, private living/bedroom spaces can be rented out individually at heavily subsidised, manageable rates.
"Shared amenities (such as kitchens, living areas, or utility spaces) maximise unit utility and reduce maintenance footprints.
"It also mitigates loneliness and isolation among elderly residents through shared community living," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt studying policy to declassify historical documents
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The government is studying a proposal to establish a general policy for the declassification of historical documents currently classified under the Official Secrets Act (OSA), to facilitate public access to such records.
Unity Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the Cabinet had agreed with views put forward by several historians on the need for such a policy.
"Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was of the view that the declassification process should be carried out promptly, but carefully," he said at a press conference after the Cabinet meeting here today.
He said the government would consult the Attorney-General's Chambers, Home Ministry and police on several related aspects.
However, he said no specific timeframe had been set for implementing the declassification process.
In a separate development, Fahmi said the government had agreed to amend the guidelines on the management of abandoned vehicles to expedite disposal procedures, which had been taking too long.
He said the decision was made after taking into account various views and complaints about the implementation of the existing guidelines.
The proposed amendments were submitted by the Transport Ministry and Housing and Local Government Ministry to improve the management and disposal processes for abandoned vehicles.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: High Court: JMB cannot impose outright ban on pets in residential units
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A joint management body (JMB) cannot impose an outright ban on keeping pets in private residential units through its house rules, the High Court ruled today.
Lawyers Rajesh Nagarajan and Sachpreetraj Singh Sohanpal, who represented former national hurdler and Olympian Noraseela Mohd Khalid, said judge Datuk Anita Harun had partially allowed her application against the JMB of Shang Villa Condominium.
In a statement, they said the court declared that House Rule 9.0 could not be used to prohibit Noraseela from keeping her three cats in her unit.
"The court held that the mere presence of pets in a residential unit did not, in itself, constitute a breach of house rules," it said.
It said any enforcement action must instead be based on By-law 14 of the Strata Management (Maintenance and Management) Regulations 2015 and supported by evidence linking the particular animal to an alleged nuisance, danger or other prohibited circumstance.
"The court decided that general complaints about animals are not enough. The court found that the evidence did not establish that Noraseela's cats were responsible for the incidents cited by the JMB.
"Her neighbour's evidence supported her account that the cats were properly cared for and veterinary certificates supported their apparent good health," they said.
Rajesh and Sachpreetraj said the court also declared invalid and unenforceable parts of House Rule 9.0 that purported to allow animals to be removed from common property without reference to their owners and exclude liability for any resulting loss.
They said, however, the court recognised that the word "may" in By-law 14 permits preventive action where there was a factual basis for concern, but management could not act on assumptions or generalised complaints.
"This judgment confirms that a JMB is not above the law. House rules cannot be used to circumvent statutory safeguards or to create powers the legislation does not confer.
"The law regulates irresponsible conduct. It does not authorise discrimination against responsible pet owners.
"Legitimate complaints about animals must be addressed, and this decision does not stand in the way of that.
"But management must act on evidence, not on a presumption that every pet is a nuisance."
They said residents of strata developments across Malaysia frequently encounter house rules that seek to prohibit pets outright, often without any assessment of the animals concerned.
"The ruling makes clear that the powers of management bodies are subject to the Strata Management Act 2013 and its prescribed by-laws, and that the preference of a majority does not justify disregarding the legal protections of individual proprietors.
"We hope the decision will encourage greater consistency and fairness in the management of strata communities.
"Responsible pet ownership and harmonious community living are not mutually exclusive, and the law requires management bodies to balance both rather than take the simplest route of banning animals."
In her suit, Noraseela argued that the
Petaling Jaya City Council (MBPJ) has no legal authority
to impose a sweeping and absolute restriction on pet ownership in apartments.
She contested the validity of MBPJ's Licensing of Dogs and Kennel Establishments By-Law 2007, claiming it conflicts with federal legislation.
She contended that Section 8(2), which prohibits residents from keeping dogs in apartment units under MBPJ's jurisdiction, exceeds the powers granted to local councils under the Local Government Act 1976 and the Strata Management Act.
Noraseela also contended that the restriction infringed residents' rights to use and enjoy their properties, and said there was no evidence that dogs or other pets had caused disturbances or nuisances to neighbours.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang tables RM1.074b budget, forecasts record-low RM5.62m deficit
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang government today tabled an operating budget of RM1.074 billion for 2027, projecting a deficit of RM5.62 million — the lowest shortfall in the state's fiscal history.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the figure marked a significant reduction from the RM19.92 million deficit
projected for 2026,
supported by steady revenue estimates and fiscal discipline.
Tabling the 2027 Penang Budget at the state legislative assembly, Chow said the state expected to collect RM1.069 billion in revenue next year, an increase of RM800,000 or 0.07 per cent from 2026.
Non-tax revenue accounts for the largest share of state receipts at RM566.11 million (52.96 per cent), derived mainly from land premiums, special charges and investment interest.
Non-revenue receipts are projected at RM277.79 million, while tax revenue is expected to contribute RM224.94 million.
"Taking into account the estimated revenue of RM1.069 billion against an estimated operating expenditure of RM1.074 billion, the 2027 Penang Budget reflects the lowest estimated deficit in the history of Penang's state budgets," he said.
Of the RM1.074 billion in operating expenditure, fixed charges and grants account for the largest portion at RM607.96 million (56.58 per cent).
This is followed by emoluments at RM231.8 million (21.58 per cent), services and supplies at RM219 million (20.38 per cent), other expenditure at RM11.38 million (1.06 per cent) and asset acquisitions at RM4.32 million (0.4 per cent).
The higher allocation for services and supplies — up by RM17.47 million or 8.67 per cent — was driven by the national minimum wage adjustment from RM1,700 to RM2,000 taking effect in June 2027, impacting state cleaning, maintenance, and security contracts.
Separately, the state has approved RM280.17 million in development expenditure for 514 projects next year, a 12.1 per cent decrease from the RM318.57 million allocated in 2026.
Chow said priority would be given to critical public connectivity projects and strategic long-term infrastructure.
"Among these are land acquisitions for the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) project, the Airport Link Road, access routes connecting to Silicon Island, Gurney Bay Phase 2, and broader components of the Penang Transport Master Plan (PTMP)," he added.
Chow said civil works under Package CMC1 of the Mutiara LRT line, covering a 23.7km stretch from Komtar to Silicon Island, had reached 15.5 per cent completion as of September 2026, with full operations scheduled for December 2031.
Other key measures announced in the budget:
*
Welfare and social safety:
The i-Sejahtera programme will retain its RM58 million allocation. A new Program Mempelai Emas will offer a one-off RM500 wedding gift to newlywed couples, while the state will establish its first Social Development Fund with an allocation of RM350,000.
*
Public transport subsidies:
A total of RM16.8 million has been allocated to subsidise public transport through Pas Mutiara and free CAT bus services. A new one-off RM600 incentive for eligible e-hailing drivers has been introduced, with an allocation ceiling of RM9 million. Taxi drivers and school bus operators will continue to receive assistance totalling RM1.2 million.
*
Quit rent relief:
The state will retain the 50 per cent rebate on quit rent in 2027, subject to eligibility criteria.
*
Industrial and technology ecosystem:
Sales of industrial plots at the 700-acre Green Tech Park on Silicon Island will begin in the first quarter of 2027, with the first production facility expected to begin operations by 2028.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Public varsities allowed to hold online classes for Deepavali break
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Public universities, polytechnics and community colleges have been allowed to conduct online or hybrid teaching and learning (PdP) sessions from Nov 5 to 13 in conjunction with the Deepavali celebration on Nov 8.
In a statement today, the Higher Education Ministry (Mohe) said the arrangement would allow Hindu students and teaching staff to return to their hometowns and spend time with their families during the festival.
"However, its implementation is subject to the suitability and requirements of the academic programmes at the respective institutions to ensure that teaching and learning processes run smoothly and academic activities are not disrupted," the statement said.
The ministry said the initiative reflected its concern for the welfare of the higher education community, while recognising the cultural and religious diversity that forms the foundation of harmony in Malaysia's multiracial society.
Mohe also extended its Deepavali greetings to all Hindu students, academic staff, ministry personnel and Malaysians.
"May this Festival of Lights bring happiness, peace and prosperity to everyone," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tabung Kasih@Hawana aid eases burden of NST journalist recovering from accident
Article:
IPOH: New Straits Times (NST) journalist Zahratulhayat Mat Arif, who was injured in an accident with Bernama journalist Nur Afiradina Arshad last Sunday, has expressed gratitude for financial assistance from Tabung Kasih@Hawana x TM.
Zahratulhayat, 37, said the contribution would help cover the costs of medical rehabilitation and psychiatric consultations following the accident on Jalan Ipoh-Lumut.
"The assistance has eased my financial burden in getting follow-up treatment. Since the accident, I have been having difficulty sleeping.
"Whenever I close my eyes, I keep recalling what happened. The accident has deeply affected me and left me traumatised," she told reporters at her home in Medan Klebang Harmoni today.
The welfare contribution was presented by Bernama Perak bureau chief Syamsiah Sahat. Also present were Perak Media Practitioners Association chairman Sayed Mohd Hesham Idris and deputy chairman Abdul Razak Mohd Ali.
Zahratulhayat said she had sought counselling at the Malaysian Mental Health Association (MMHA) Perak in Bercham to cope with the trauma.
"The assistance came at the right time as I have to pay for the counselling sessions," said Zahratulhayat, who has been with NST for 11 years.
She also thanked those who had offered assistance and continued encouragement, including fellow media practitioners in Perak.
Meanwhile, Sayed Mohd Hesham said the assistance reflected the Communications Ministry's and the Madani government's concern for the welfare of media practitioners.
He said the timely contribution would help Zahratulhayat meet the costs of her recovery, adding that he hoped both journalists would recover soon and return to work.
On Tuesday, Nur Afiradina, who has nearly five years of journalism experience, also received financial assistance from Tabung Kasih@Hawana x TM to help with her medical expenses.
The contribution was presented by Bernama chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, accompanied by the agency's senior management, at Nur Afiradina's home in Semenyih, Selangor.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the ministry, through Bernama, acted promptly to provide assistance to both journalists.
Tabung Kasih@Hawana x TM is an extension of the Tabung Kasih@Hawana initiative, supported by Telekom Malaysia's corporate social responsibility funding to assist more media practitioners in need.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singaporean fan makes annual Karnival Jom Heboh trip despite mobility challenges
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A stroke in February did not deter a loyal Singaporean TV3 fan from attending Karnival Jom Heboh 2026 at Padang B, Angsana Johor Bahru Mall here today.
Jannah Naz Abdullah, 50, said she has never missed attending the iconic carnival since its inaugural edition in Bukit Jalil, Kuala Lumpur, in 2003.
She said although her mobility was affected after the stroke, it did not stop her from travelling from Singapore with her family to experience the atmosphere.
"I came from Singapore solely to attend KJH. I suffered a stroke in February and cannot walk as well as before, but the determination to come here remains.
"I took a bus from Jurong to Tuas before continuing the journey to Gelang Patah with my husband and child," she said.
Jannah Naz said her visit to KJH was not merely for shopping, but served as an opportunity to spend quality time with family and friends.
She said apart from the wide variety of food and performances, the warm hospitality of booth crews and personalities was among the main attractions keeping her coming back.
She said she will be in Johor Baru until Sunday and plans to visit KJH again on Saturday and Sunday.
Meanwhile, the carnival also drew housewife Ain Shafiqah Zakaria, 25, from Kempas, who attended with her husband and child.
She said this year's edition was livelier, with numerous sales booths offering goods at affordable prices.
"KJH this time is the best because there are many sales and booths. I am taking the opportunity to buy bargain items while spending quality time with my family.
"This is my second time attending KJH, and I hope this carnival will continue in the future," she said.
KJH Johor Bahru 2026 offers various activities, including sales booths, performances by local artistes, family-oriented events, and daily essentials promotions.
Recognised as the Longest Running Outdoor Carnival by the Malaysia Book of Records, the event runs for three days until Sunday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang civil servants to receive one-month bonus in December
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang civil servants will receive a special financial assistance equivalent to one month's salary, payable in December, the state legislative assembly was told today.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the incentive was a token of appreciation for the dedication and integrity demonstrated by the state public sector workforce.
"The state's fiscal strength and development achievements could not have been attained without the backing of an efficient, high-integrity and high-performing administrative machinery," he said when tabling the 2027 Penang Budget.
"As a token of appreciation to all members of the state civil service, I am pleased to announce a special financial assistance of one month's salary," he added.
Chow said one-off payments of RM300 would also be given to supervisors and teachers of Quran and Fardu Ain (Kafa) classes, staff of Islamic religious primary and secondary schools, government-aided religious schools, tahfiz and pondok institutions.
This also includes staff in Islamic kindergartens, as well as teachers and staff of Chinese private schools in Penang.
The payments would cost the state RM16.207 million and benefit 7,292 recipients.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM30 million allocated for Media Innovation Fund 2.0
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The government has allocated RM30 million for the Media Innovation Fund 2.0 to support the transformation and growth of the local media industry.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the initiative would help media companies strengthen their operations and explore new approaches to content production and delivery.
"The Madani government will continue the Media Innovation Fund initiative through the implementation of Media Innovation Fund 2.0, with an allocation of RM30 million.
"The initiative reflects the government's ongoing commitment to ensuring the media industry continues to be strengthened, particularly in innovation, digitalisation, talent development and the adoption of new technologies," he said at a post-cabinet meeting press conference.
Fahmi said the latest fund retained the four existing funding categories while introducing a new one, bringing the total to five.
The new category covers subscriptions to news services and media content.
The four existing categories are training for media personnel; software and technology adoption; equipment, hardware and support facilities; and content research and development.
The fund aims to help local media organisations strengthen their digital transformation through training, the adoption of new technologies and software, equipment upgrades and content development.
In the previous edition, 72 media companies received funding for various transformation initiatives, including training, strengthening their operations and exploring new approaches to content production and delivery.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Affordable books key to nurturing young readers in Sabah
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Making books more affordable and accessible is key to encouraging children to develop reading habits, think critically and explore new ideas.
Sabah Chief Minister's special officer Yee Tsai Yiew said access to books could help shape the next generation by encouraging children to question, imagine and broaden their understanding of the world.
"I believe most of us can remember a book that left a lasting impression on us, perhaps even changing the way we see the world.
"Perhaps that is where changing the world begins, by encouraging the next generation to pick up a book.
"When we encourage children to read, we encourage them to think, to question, to imagine and to discover what is possible," she said at the launch of Big Bad Wolf Books at the Sabah International Convention Centre here.
Yee said the state government welcomed initiatives that supported education, lifelong learning and community development, and hoped similar efforts would reach more communities across Sabah.
She added that this year's book sale coincided with the Big Sabah Sale 2026, bringing more visitors to Kota Kinabalu while supporting the local economy.
Big Bad Wolf Books Kota Kinabalu 2026, featuring more than one million books, runs until Nov 9.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka MACC opens 24-hour operations room ahead of election
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) in Melaka will set up a 24-hour operations room to receive public information and complaints on corruption and abuse of power during the Melaka election.
In a statement today, MACC said the operations room, located at its office in Taman Alai Perdana, would operate round the clock from tomorrow until polling day on Nov 14.
"The public may submit any information or complaints throughout the election process via email at prnmlk@sprm.gov.my, by contacting the MACC Melaka office line at 06-2896000, the operations room at 06-2896303, or the 24-hour hotline/WhatsApp number at 011-26791569," the statement read.
MACC also reminded all candidates, political parties, supporters and other parties involved in the 16th Melaka election to refrain from actions that violate election laws and regulations, in accordance with the MACC Act 2009 and the Election Offences Act 1954.
The Election Commission (EC) has set Nov 14 as polling day, with candidate nomination scheduled for tomorrow and early voting on Nov 10.
The Melaka State Legislative Assembly was dissolved effective Sept 23, following the consent of Yang Dipertua Negeri of Melaka Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Fence-sitters hold key to victory, says Rafizi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The outcome of the Melaka election is likely to be determined by fence-sitters rather than avid supporters of any political party, says Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) leader Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli.
He said supporters of each major coalition were estimated to make up only a relatively small proportion of the electorate.
Based on current estimates, Rafizi said, Barisan Nasional supporters account for about 20 to 21 per cent, Pakatan Harapan 18 to 19 per cent, and Perikatan Nasional 17 to 18 per cent.
Bersama, meanwhile, is estimated to have about 10 per cent support.
"Secara keseluruhannya, jumlah gabungan penyokong tegar kesemua parti berkenaan hanya sekitar 70 peratus.
"Overall, avid supporters of these parties account for only about 70 per cent of the electorate. Based on this calculation, the remaining 25 to 30 per cent are fence-sitters.
"This is particularly true among Malay voters, making them the decisive group that could determine which coalition wins," he said in the latest episode of the Yang Berhenti Menteri (YBM) podcast.
Rafizi, a former PKR deputy president, said the political leanings of Malay fence-sitters had consistently shifted in response to prevailing sentiments.
He said issues such as the cost of living, the Goods and Services Tax (GST), the 1MDB scandal and Umno's leadership problems had prompted more than 20 per cent of Malay voters to switch their support to PH in the 14th General Election.
However, dissatisfaction with the PH administration later saw the so-called silent majority split and shift towards PN in 2022, driven by a desire to try a new alternative rather than a sudden surge in avid Pas supporters, he said.
As Melaka heads towards its state election, Rafizi said Malay fence-sitters appeared to be leaning towards the sentiment of "Malay-Muslim unity" amid prolonged political infighting.
"Conversely, issues of governance, 'sakau' and integrity raised by PH are seen as losing their impact and failing to resonate emotionally with voters
"Fence-sitters are beginning to perceive all political parties as being tainted by similar issues following recent controversies and integrity-related concerns," he said.
On non-Malay voters, Rafizi said the current political landscape had also opened the door to a reassessment of their political preferences.
He said Umno's treatment of MCA within BN could hurt the feelings of Chinese and Indian voters and remind them of the reasons they had previously rejected the coalition.
At the same time, he said, PKR and Amanah appeared willing to consider cooperation with Malay-based parties such as Bersatu.
"This includes the decision to give up the Bemban state seat, as announced by PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
"The decision has raised questions about the consistency of the coalition's principles.
"This could also open up the possibility of political realignments between the major coalitions in the future," he said.
Meanwhile, Rafizi said Bersama appeared to be receiving positive feedback from fence-sitters because of its image as a party that was hardworking, consistent and focused on serving the people rather than pursuing power.
However, he said, its ability to translate that perception into actual votes would only become clear after its candidates were announced and a week of campaigning had taken place.
He added that the success of parties contesting in Melaka would largely depend on their ability to balance national-level policy narratives and positions with concrete local proposals in their respective manifestos.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCMC awarded RM15.3mil liquidated damages over delayed Sabah Jendela project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court in Shah Alam has ordered a contractor to pay RM15.32 million in liquidated damages to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for failing to complete works under the National Digital Network (Jendela) project in Sabah within the agreed timeframe.
The court also ordered MajuBina Resources Sdn Bhd to pay RM5,000 in costs to MCMC.
In a statement today, MCMC said the court had granted a summary judgment in its favour for RM15,324,832.31.
MCMC filed the lawsuit in February to recover liquidated damages arising from delays in carrying out works under Jendela Phase 1, which is part of the Universal Service Provision (USP) initiative.
The initiative aims to expand the coverage and accessibility of communications services, particularly in rural and underserved areas.
MCMC said all communications infrastructure projects funded through the USP fund must comply with contractual obligations and agreed timelines.
"Compliance with these requirements is essential to ensure projects are implemented smoothly and that the benefits of digital connectivity reach the public, particularly those in rural and underserved areas," it said.
The commission said the court's decision underscored the importance of accountability in implementing the country's communications infrastructure projects.
It added that it would continue to ensure USP funds were used responsibly to improve public access to quality communications services.
In December 2024, Bernama reported that Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor had been informed by MCMC that only 217 of the 382 Jendela Phase 1 towers in Sabah, or 57 per cent, had been completed.
In a separate report that month, Bernama quoted Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching as saying that a Non-Compliance Notice had been issued on Oct 28, 2024, to all Phase 1 and Phase 2 Designated Universal Service Providers that had yet to complete their Jendela projects.
She had also warned that contractors who failed to meet the deadlines could face measures including liquidated damages.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: More than 6.5 tonnes of chicken seized over suspected halal violations in Puchong
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken suspected of being processed without complying with halal certification standards were seized during a midnight raid on a Puchong warehouse yesterday.
Twelve Bangladeshi and Pakistani men, believed to be involved in slaughtering and processing poultry at the premises, were also detained during the operation, codenamed Op Taring Chiller.
Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department Wildlife Crime Control Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said the raid, conducted at 12.40am, uncovered premises suspected of being used to slaughter, process, and distribute fresh chicken without valid halal certification.
He said preliminary inspections revealed slaughtering and handling practices that raised serious concerns over compliance with Islamic requirements and the halal status of the products.
"Inspections found that the chickens were believed to have been immersed in hot water until they died before being slaughtered," he said in a statement today.
The integrated operation was carried out in collaboration with the Selangor Islamic Religious Department, Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim), Department of Environment, and Petaling District Health Office.
Zaki said authorities seized 468 plastic packages containing raw chicken weighing approximately 6,555kg, with an estimated value of RM85,400.
Preliminary investigations indicated that the premises had allegedly been operating as a chicken slaughtering, processing, and distribution centre for some time, with supplies sourced from several poultry farms around Sepang.
"The processed chicken was believed to have been distributed to customers, including restaurants, grocery shops and supermarkets across the Klang Valley," he said.
The case is being investigated under Sections 3(1)(a) and 4(1) of the Trade Descriptions (Definition of Halal) Order 2011 and Section 38(1) of the Environmental Quality Act 1974.
The 12 foreigners are also being investigated under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 and Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penampang road upgrades to improve access to 3 schools
Article:
PENAMPANG: Three schools in Penampang will benefit from road upgrades in Buayan and Terian, with both projects progressing ahead of schedule, said Datuk Ewon Benedick.
The Penampang member of parliament said the improved roads would benefit SK Terian, SK Buayan and SK Longkogungan, located about 12km away, as well as about 3,000 residents in four villages.
"There are two schools in this area, namely SK Terian and SK Buayan.
"Another school is located about 12km from here, namely SK Longkogungan. This means three schools will benefit from these road facilities," he said during a work visit.
Ewon said some villagers, teachers and students currently have to travel on foot because of poor road access.
The upgraded roads are also expected to support agricultural and tourism activities in Kampung Terian, Kampung Tiku, Kampung Buayan and Kampung Longkogungan.
A previous NST report highlighted how
volunteers
had to hike through dense forests to deliver aid to villages in the area.
The RM73.868 million Buayan road upgrade project is 76.64 per cent complete and is 45 days ahead of schedule, with completion expected in August 2027.
The RM99.395 million Terian road upgrade project is 57.83 per cent complete and is 58 days ahead of its revised schedule after being granted an extension of time until May 2028.
Ewon, who is also Sabah Deputy Chief Minister III and Industrial Development, Entrepreneurship and Transport Minister, thanked the Federal Government, Finance Ministry and Rural and Regional Development Ministry for funding and implementing the projects.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Heavy rain forecast for east coast, Johor and Sarawak until January
Article:
PUCHONG: Kelantan and Terengganu are expected to experience continuous heavy rain in November, followed by Pahang and Johor in December, and Sarawak in January, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said.
Its National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre senior director Maqrun Fadzli Mohd Fahmi said three to five episodes of continuous heavy rain were expected between November and January during the early phase of the northeast monsoon.
He was presenting the department's outlook at a media engagement session on the government's monsoon preparations at the Special Malaysia Search and Rescue Team (Smart) headquarters here.
Also present were National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim, Malaysian Civil Defence Force deputy chief commissioner (operations) Ghazali Abdul Rahman and Smart commander Abdul Manaf Che Isa.
The monsoon began on Oct 27 and is expected to last until mid-March.
Maqrun said warnings of continuous rain, strong winds and rough seas would be issued up to three days in advance.
The risk of major floods would increase if prolonged heavy rain coincided with high tides.
Despite the expected heavy-rain episodes, total monsoon rainfall is forecast to be below the climatological average, particularly in the northern peninsula, Perak, Sabah and parts of Pahang and Kelantan.
Maqrun also said El Niño had reached a strong level by September and was expected to exceed 2.0°C, reaching the "super" level, by the end of the year.
The phenomenon is expected to persist until mid-2027.
During the 2015/16 super El Niño, rainfall during the monsoon fell by 30 per cent in the peninsula and 45 per cent in Sabah, while Sarawak did not experience a significant decline.
Several states are also forecast to receive below-average rainfall in specific months.
These include southern Johor and eastern Sabah in October, and Sabah from November to March.
Perlis and Kedah are expected to receive less rainfall from January to March, while Penang and Perak are forecast to see a similar trend from February to March.
In March, Kelantan, Pahang, Labuan, Sabah and Sarawak are expected to receive slightly below-average rainfall.
Southern Sarawak, however, is expected to receive slightly above-average rainfall in January.
From January to March, rainfall is expected to decline further, particularly in the northern states and Sabah, bringing hotter and drier conditions with the potential for more extreme heatwaves.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nadma warns unprepared, low-risk areas pose biggest threat this monsoon
Article:
PUCHONG: The areas of the country that rarely experience floods are the biggest concern ahead of this year's Northeast Monsoon, despite forecasts indicating that flooding will be at its lowest level, says the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma).
Its director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said areas accustomed to flooding generally had better response mechanisms in place, while less frequently affected areas might be less prepared.
"Based on the forecast so far, we think this year's floods will be the lowest. We pray the forecast is right," he said.
He was speaking at a press conference during a media engagement session at the Special Malaysia Search and Rescue Team (Smart) headquarters here.
Also present were Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre senior director Maqrun Fadzli Mohd Fahmi, Malaysian Civil Defence Force (CDF) deputy chief commissioner (operations) Ghazali Abdul Rahman and Smart commander Abdul Manaf Che Isa.
According to Nadma's presentation, 101,901 personnel from five agencies are on standby, alongside 8,321 temporary evacuation centres (PPS) with a combined capacity of 1,907,145 people.
The number of flood hotspots has also declined to 3,045 this year, compared with 5,648 in 2023.
Nadma has set aside 60,000 food kits and 170,000 retort meals for distribution.
Meor Ismail, who has been involved in managing monsoon floods for almost five years, said his greatest concern was areas that rarely experienced flooding.
"What worries me most are areas that rarely flood.
"In areas that usually flood, when I visit, I see the responses are good, with the district office, health department officials, Fire and Rescue Department and Civil Defence all used to it. In new areas, I'm more worried," he said.
He stressed that a lower flood forecast did not mean preparations could be scaled back.
"I've issued the same instruction to the agencies," he said, adding that some might otherwise become complacent.
Meor Ismail said Nadma had not identified any new flood-prone areas for this season.
"We prepare all the usual areas. I have also instructed that even places that don't flood must be ready," he said.
[[nid:1567019]]
'Move early'
He advised residents in flood-prone areas to evacuate early once MetMalaysia issued its three-day forecast.
"I'm not saying 100 per cent, but when MetMalaysia's three-day forecast comes out, it is very nearly right, so we hope people act," he said.
He said those with vehicles should evacuate on their own, while people with disabilities, young children and expectant mothers should be prioritised for early evacuation.
"When a rescue boat comes, each carries only about 10 people.
"If a housing area floods with 1,000 residents, how many boats would you need? That's why we say, if you get the information, move early," he said.
'Preparations in place'
Meor Ismail said Nadma had added permanent relief centres this year and introduced community-based disaster risk management programmes in several states.
Almost all state disaster command centres were also now in place.
He said assets such as boats had been positioned in areas where flooding was expected, while assistance could reach other locations within 24 hours.
Local leaders and village heads were often the first responders, he said, adding that the Fire and Rescue Department usually allowed fishermen's associations on the East Coast to assist in rescue operations.
Meor Ismail declined to disclose the locations of the 3,045 flood hotspots, citing potential implications.
"I don't want to be specific. Hotspots have other implications, and sometimes we can't state where they are.
"I'd rather not say, because there can be implications," he said.
He said residents were familiar with the hotspots as areas that regularly experienced flooding, and that the relevant agencies were aware of them and had made preparations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit extends gains against US dollar as traders reassess Fed rate outlook
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The ringgit extended its gains to close higher against the US dollar today as traders reassessed the possibility of an interest rate hike by the US Federal Reserve (Fed), an analyst said.
The Fed decided to keep the benchmark interest rate steady at 3.75 per cent to 4.00 per cent on Oct 28.
At 6 pm, the ringgit rose to 4.0555/0600 against the greenback from yesterday’s close of 4.0575/0620.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the dollar-ringgit was seen to be at around RM4.0425 during the morning session but later moved towards RM4.0577, giving a 0.05 per cent gain against the dollar.
“It appears that traders are reassessing the likelihood of a rate hike, which has led to lower US Dollar Index (DXY) by 0.32 per cent to 101.710 points,” he told
Bernama.
Against major currencies, the ringgit eased against the British pound to 5.4461/4522 from 5.4009/4069 at Thursday’s close, slid against the euro to 4.5413/5464 from 4.5176/5226, and weakened vis-a-vis the Japanese yen to 2.5782/5812 from 2.5685/5715 previously.
The ringgit was also mostly lower against its Asean peers.
It gained vis-a-vis the Indonesian rupiah to 223.4/223.8 from yesterday’s close of 223.7/224.0, but slipped against the Singapore dollar to 3.1753/1791 from 3.1665/1702 previously.
It also lost against the Thai baht to 12.0373/0561 from 12.0165/0345 at yesterday’s close, and inched down vis-a-vis the Philippine peso at 6.36/6.37 from 6.35/6.36 previously. — Bernama

Title: Sabah defence upgrades not a response to Philippine military build-up, says Khaled
Article:
LABUAN, Oct 30 — Malaysia will continue strengthening its military capabilities in Sabah to safeguard national security amid regional geopolitical developments, but the move is not a direct response to the Philippines’ military build-up on Balabac Island, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said.
He said every country has the right to enhance its defence capabilities, and Malaysia was similarly committed to ensuring its armed forces remained prepared for any potential escalation of regional tensions.
“Every country has the right to strengthen its military capabilities, and Malaysia will do the same. However, our efforts are not a reaction to what the Philippines is doing in its southern region, but part of our preparations to ensure that any escalation of tensions will have minimal impact on Malaysia,” he told reporters after receiving the FA-50M aircrafts from South Korea at the Labuan Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) base here.
Khaled was commenting on the Philippine government’s efforts to strengthen military facilities on Balabac Island in southern Palawan, which has been designated as a military cooperation site accessible to the United States forces.
Khaled said strengthening Malaysia’s defence capabilities, particularly in Sabah, remained a key priority of the Defence Ministry.
He said the ministry would determine the number of FA-50M light combat aircraft to be stationed at the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) base in Labuan following the planned decommissioning of Hawk fighter aircraft in 2028.
“Once the Hawk aircraft are phased out in 2028, we will determine how many FA-50M aircraft will be stationed at the Labuan air base,” he said.
He said the government had also decided to install new radar systems in Sabah, including on Layang-Layang Island, to enhance surveillance and early detection capabilities.
“The ministry would also increase military personnel in Sabah, where more than 10,000 troops are currently stationed, while new military camps have been developed to strengthen operational readiness,” he said.
Khaled reiterated that the initiatives were part of Malaysia’s continuing efforts to reinforce national defence and protect its sovereignty, rather than a response to military developments in neighbouring countries. — Bernama

Title: The more, the merrier? State Pakatan chairman says crowded Melaka races could work in coalition’s favour
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 30 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) does not regard multi-cornered contests in the Melaka state election as a disadvantage, saying a crowded field could instead create more opportunities for the coalition to secure victories.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said a straight fight did not necessarily give a party an advantage, as three- or four-cornered contests could, in certain circumstances, offer better prospects from a strategic standpoint.
“Based on my experience in previous four-cornered contests, having more candidates is not necessarily an obstacle to winning. Instead, it can create opportunities that contesting parties can take advantage of.
“There are certainly challenges as well as advantages in terms of our strategy. Sometimes, a straight fight can be more difficult than a three-cornered contest,” he told reporters after a tea reception with Melaka media practitioners in Ayer Keroh here today.
Also present was Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim.
Adly said PH’s decision to increase the number of seats it is contesting from 21 to 24 was also made after assessing the current political landscape and the coalition’s prospects of winning.
He said the coalition had initially settled on contesting 21 seats on October 24 before reviewing its position and identifying further opportunities to strengthen its chances.
The decision, he said, should not be interpreted as a failure in negotiations with any political party, as PH had made its assessment based on its own capabilities and prevailing political developments.
He said another principle taken into consideration was to ensure that no state constituency was won uncontested, allowing voters to exercise their democratic right to choose their representatives.
“For example, when we realised that Bersatu was not fielding a candidate in a particular seat, that decision had been made without consulting us.
“So we stepped in to ensure the democratic process could proceed as it should. Voters must be given the opportunity to make their choice,” he said.
Nominations will take place tomorrow, with early voting on November 10 and polling on November 14. — Bernama

Title: MOF never ordered rural road projects cancelled, only deferred new contracts, says Tengku Zafrul
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The Finance Ministry (MOF) has never issued any directive to cancel rural road projects, but has only deferred new contracts to prevent outstanding payments to contractors from continuing to accumulate, according to the prime minister’s senior political adviser, Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz.
He said the deferment was necessary following rural road development expenditure exceeding the original allocations approved by Parliament annually since 2022, resulting in increased contractual commitments and outstanding payments to contractors.
“The deferment of new contracts does not mean existing projects have been cancelled. MOF has never issued any directive to cancel projects. New contracts were deferred to prevent outstanding payments from continuing to increase.
“These are two different things. That is why the country’s finances must be managed prudently, not merely by approving projects but also by ensuring sufficient allocations are available to pay for them,” he said in a video shared on his social media today.
Tengku Zafrul said claims that rural road allocations, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak, had been deliberately reduced should be assessed based on the government’s actual expenditure figures for the period concerned.
He said rural road expenditure for the 2023-2027 period, including allocations for this year and next year, had increased to RM11 billion compared with RM3.7 billion for the 2018-2022 period, representing almost a threefold increase.
“In Sabah and Sarawak alone, actual rural road expenditure this year reached RM1.41 billion, the highest in the past 10 years.
“Since 2023, RM4.6 billion has been spent. Every year, approximately half of the country’s total rural road expenditure is channelled to Sabah and Sarawak. Sabah and Sarawak have not been sidelined. Sabah and Sarawak have been given priority,” he said.
Tengku Zafrul said MOF had to balance the allocation needs of all ministries, including those responsible for health, education and rural development, to ensure the government’s financial commitments could be met.
He said when a ministry made spending commitments that exceeded its approved allocation, MOF had to seek additional financial resources to meet those requirements.
In this regard, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had approved an additional RM500 million in expenditure for 2026, using savings from the development allocations of other ministries, to enable outstanding payments to contractors to be settled.
He said the government understood that many villages in Sabah and Sarawak were still waiting for better road facilities.
