In this connection, Budget 2027 provides RM2.27 billion for rural road development, while RM34.9 billion has been allocated to Sabah and Sarawak, the highest amount among all states.
He also reminded all parties that development issues in the two states should not be used as political ammunition.
“As the prime minister has stressed, allocations alone are not enough without good governance. What matters is that projects are implemented, contractors are paid and the people benefit. That is our priority,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Saris, sweets and shopping sprees: Deepavali buzz builds across Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The festive atmosphere ahead of Deepavali on November 8 is becoming more vibrant as the Indian community nationwide begins making preparations for the Festival of Lights, including purchasing traditional attire, preparing special delicacies and decorating their homes to celebrate the occasion with family and relatives.
Bernama’s survey in several states found that shopping hotspots are beginning to draw crowds purchasing festive essentials, while traders are offering a wide selection of goods and special promotions to attract customers.
In
KUALA LUMPUR
, traders in Little India, Brickfields, are hoping for an increase in visitors this weekend, although the recent unpredictable weather has somewhat affected sales.
Shoe and accessories trader Vishan Daren, 30, said the rain had resulted in fewer customers, but visitor numbers have started to pick up today and are expected to increase further on Saturday and Sunday.
In
SELANGOR
, a survey at Little India, Klang, found that Deepavali preparations had also attracted people from various ethnic communities, including Nadia Dastghill, 44, who was shopping for traditional Indian attire for her child’s school celebration and a sari as a gift for the teacher.
Another visitor, N. Rama Rao, 38, said Little India remains his family’s preferred shopping destination as it offers a wide selection of traditional attire at reasonable prices.
Deepavali preparations are gathering pace in Ipoh, with traders hoping for a rise in customers over the weekend. — Bernama pic
In
NEGERI SEMBILAN
, about 30,000 visitors are expected to throng the Deepavali Bazaar at Jalan Datuk Lee Fong Yee, popularly known as Little India Seremban, throughout its 10-day operation, which began yesterday.
Negeri Sembilan Indian Community Affairs special officer Datuk VS Mogan said the bazaar features 140 traders offering a variety of festive goods, as well as performances by local artistes, including Santesh Kumar, to enliven the atmosphere.
In
JOHOR
, members of the public have begun making early preparations by visiting the Deepavali Bazaar along Jalan Ungku Puan in Johor Bahru to purchase traditional attire, decorative flowers, accessories, as well as various sweets and snacks.
Homemaker K. Kalaivani, 40, from Pasir Gudang, said she chose to shop a week in advance to avoid the last-minute crowds.
Meanwhile, traditional snack trader Renuka, 34, said customer response has been encouraging so far, with tarts,
suji
and
murukku
among the most sought-after festive delicacies.
Shoppers browse traditional attire, accessories and festive decorations ahead of Deepavali in Johor Bahru October 30, 2026. — Bernama pic
In
PENANG
, the festive excitement ahead of Deepavali is evident, with business premises adorned with colourful decorations and offering special sales and discounts on selected items.
VKN Sivasamy & Son director Aditya Tandian said customer response is almost on par with last year’s, with some visitors coming from Sungai Petani, Kulim, Ipoh and Kuala Lumpur, while about 10 to 15 per cent of customers made their purchases online.
In
PERLIS
, V. Malarvizhi, 56, a vendor selling festive goods in Pauh, Arau, said customer response remains slow but is expected to pick up about a week before Deepavali, as people begin shopping for clothes, religious items and traditional delicacies.
Malarvizhi, who has been in the business for more than 10 years, said most customers typically made their purchases in the final week before the festival, while she would make her own preparations three to four days before Deepavali.
Colourful ‘saris’, ‘kurtas’ and festive accessories are among the goods attracting shoppers ahead of the Festival of Lights. — Bernama pic
In
PAHANG
, Dr S. Bavani, 43, from Kuantan, said her family’s preparations begin with purchasing traditional attire such as
saris
and
kurtas
, as well as preparing traditional delicacies, including
murukku
and sweets, to serve guests.
The mother of two said cleaning and decorating the house with oil lamps and colourful ornaments are also part of the preparations to create a festive atmosphere.
Meanwhile, in
KELANTAN
, the Hindu community in Kuala Krai and Tanah Merah is making modest preparations while maintaining traditions such as preparing festive delicacies, cleaning their homes and strengthening family and neighbourhood ties.
Single mother of seven, R. Parvathy, 68, from Kuala Krai, said her children helped purchase traditional attire and other festive necessities, while she prepared
murukku
to be shared with family members and neighbours.
Another Tanah Merah resident, S. Chandrakala, 40, said preparing traditional delicacies such as murukku and laddu with family members not only added to the festive cheer but also ensured that the heritage continued to be preserved by younger generations. — Bernama
Traditional Deepavali delicacies, including ‘murukku’, ‘laddu’ and ‘suji’, are among the popular purchases as families prepare for the celebrations. — Bernama pic

Title: Rubbish raid! Thirteen-foot crocodile caught after rummaging through trash for food in Sarawak village
Article:
KOTA SAMARAHAN, Oct 30 — A crocodile measuring over 13 feet (about 3.96m) was captured this morning following reports of the reptile roaming in the area and posing a potential safety concern for nearby villagers.
Licensed crocodile capture team Sarawak Crocter said in a Facebook post that the operation was carried out in collaboration with the Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC).
“The crocodile has gone viral recently and has now been captured for the sake of the villagers’ safety.
“Please report any dangerous crocodile sightings to the authorities as soon as possible,” the post read.
Meanwhile, licensed crocodile hunter Jeferry Siew said in a separate post that the reptile had been spotted in the area two days earlier, rummaging through rubbish for food. — The Borneo Post

Title: Bought one thing, got another? Anwar orders crackdown on online shopping scams, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) and the Communications Ministry, through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), to take immediate action against fraud and scams on e-commerce platforms.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the directive followed Anwar’s concerns over problems faced by online shoppers and sellers, including high commission fees imposed on merchants and customers receiving products that did not match their orders.
“The prime minister raised concerns about the problems faced by e-commerce users, particularly high fees and commissions charged to sellers, as well as customers receiving products that differ from what they ordered.
“He has therefore instructed KPDN and the Communications Ministry, particularly through MCMC, to take action on several issues, especially fraud and scams on e-commerce platforms,” he told a press conference after the Cabinet meeting here today.
He said MCMC had met representatives of all major e-commerce platforms several weeks ago to discuss the issues.
Fahmi said that a retreat involving enforcement agencies would be held in the coming weeks to coordinate an integrated response to problems affecting e-commerce users.
“The prime minister has directed that this matter be prioritised and addressed urgently.
“Insya-Allah, I will make several additional announcements on the issue tomorrow during the National Courier Day celebration,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Sale of first industrial plots on Silicon Island to start in Q1 2027, says Penang CM
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 30 — The Penang government hopes to sell the first industrial plots on Silicon Island as early as the first quarter of 2027, said Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow.
He said the development on Silicon Island will focus on the 700-acre Green Tech Park which is planned as a green, smart and sustainable high-tech industrial hub in line with environmental, social and governance (ESG) principles.
“The sale of the first industrial plots is expected to begin as early as the first quarter of 2027 to attract high-value investments, particularly in the semiconductor, automated test equipment, integrated circuit design and medical device sectors,” he said when tabling the Supply Bill at the state legislative assembly today.
He said the first factory in the Green Tech Park is expected to begin operations by 2028 while creating high-skilled employment opportunities for Penangites.
“The development of Silicon Island is not merely about providing new land for industry, but is also a long-term investment that generates benefits for the local economy,” he said.
He said a total of 4,531 contracts worth RM1.92 billion had been awarded to local contractors and businesses as of September 30.
On the development of Silicon Island, he said a total of 500 acres had been reclaimed, equivalent to 39.4 per cent of the 1,270-acre Phase 1 as of October.
In May this year, he said a 64.85-acre site was also prepared for the Mutiara Line LRT depot.

Title: Repairs on Kuching’s Jalan Lapangan Terbang water main completed, supply restoration in stages, says Sarawak Water
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 30 — Emergency repair works on a critical 750mm mild steel cement-lined (MSCL) water main on Jalan Lapangan Terbang were completed at 2am today, said Sarawak Water Sdn Bhd.
The utility provider said water supply restoration is now underway in stages.
It said the unscheduled water supply interruption was necessitated by repair works on the 750mm pipeline located off Jalan Kuching Ranger Depot after it was damaged by third-party operations associated with the Kuching Urban Transportation System (KUTS) project.
The disruption affected consumers in the Datuk Muda Tank supply area, Jalan Lapangan Terbang, Jalan Tun Jugah, Jalan Batu Lintang, and surrounding areas.
The company had initially estimated the interruption to last from 4.30pm on October 29 until 5am on October 30.
In a progress update issued at 11.45pm yesterday, the utility provider said the leak location had been identified and repair crews were dewatering the site to facilitate repair works.
Following completion of the repair works at 2am, Sarawak Water said valve reopening and network pressurisation had commenced, with water supply expected to be restored gradually.
Consumers in higher-elevation areas or those located towards the end of distribution lines may experience a longer delay before normal water pressure is fully restored.
The company also cautioned that consumers might temporarily experience discoloured or muddy water, as well as milky-looking water, when supply resumed.
It explained that sediment dislodged from the pipelines could cause temporary discolouration, while trapped air bubbles could give the water a milky appearance.
Consumers are advised to run their external taps for a few minutes until the water becomes completely clear before using it for cooking, drinking, or washing.
Sarawak Water also advised consumers in the affected areas to use water wisely and thanked residents and businesses for their patience and understanding throughout the emergency repair operation.
The utility provider said it would continue monitoring the distribution system as water supply recovery progresses. — The Borneo Post

Title: Penang Budget 2027 sets aside RM600 aid for e-hailing drivers, RM500 for newlyweds
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 30 — E-hailing drivers will be getting a special one-off incentive of RM600 in 2027 under the newly tabled state Budget 2027.
Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the special incentive is in recognition of the welfare of those working in the public transport sector.
“This is for eligible drivers in 2027 with an allocation ceiling of RM9 million,” he said when tabling the Supply Bill at the state legislative assembly today.
He said there will also be an allocation of RM1.2 million for taxi drivers and school bus operators in 2027.
As for the incentives for newlyweds, he said the Mempelai Emas programme is an expansion of the i-Sejahtera programme as a form of appreciation for couples who have recently married in Penang.
“Couples who meet the eligibility requirements will receive a one-off contribution of RM500,”  he said.
He said the state government had disbursed RM57.8 million through the implementation of the first and second phases of the i-Sejahtera programme as at September 30.
The programme benefited a total 299,504 recipients, particularly senior citizens, persons with disabilities, single mothers and housewives.
He added that the addition of the Mempelai Emas programme is also included in the state’s annual allocation of RM58 million for the i-Sejahtera programme in 2027.
Meanwhile, he said the state government is also examining changes in the structure of society and current housing needs.
He said there is a growing need for housing involving single people and senior citizens living alone.
“As such, in 2027, the Penang State Housing Board (LPNPP) will explore the co-living concept for suitable state government rental housing and People’s Housing Programme units,” he said.
Chow said the state will be introducing a Penang State Social Development Fund for the first time in 2027 with an allocation of RM350,000.
“The fund will support the implementation of various welfare and social development initiatives, particularly to assist those in need, address poverty and social inequality, and empower vulnerable groups so that they are not left behind in the state’s development,” he said.

Title: Indonesian woman fined RM4,000 and ordered deported over RM100 sex offer to undercover cop in Kuching
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 30 — An Indonesian woman was fined RM4,000 in default six months in jail by the Magistrates’ Court here for soliciting sexual services from an undercover policeman for RM100.
Magistrate Nureina Syafika Mohd Najib imposed the sentence against Pita, 37, after she pleaded guilty to a charge under Section 372B of the Penal Code.
According to the charge, Pita committed the offence at a beauty and health centre on Jalan Batu Kawa here at around 5pm on October 27.
Based on the facts of the case, police conducted an inspection at the premises to detect prostitution activities following information received from an undercover police agent, who had been instructed to carry out the operation.
During the inspection of an unnumbered room, police found Pita with the undercover agent and arrested her for further action.
Items seized to assist for the investigation included a bottle of massage oil, an unused condom, a packet of wet wipes, and RM100.
Investigations found that Pita had offered sexual services to the undercover agent for a cash payment of RM100.
Pita also pleaded guilty to an immigration offence for being in Malaysia without a valid pass, under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
Judge Mursyida Abd Halim sentenced her to four months in prison, effective October 30 and ordered that she be deported to her home country upon completion of her sentence.
The two charges were prosecuted separately by deputy public prosecutors Ahmad Fauzulutfi Suriani and Marvind Kaliyani.
Pita did not have legal representation. — The Borneo Post

Title: Penang tables RM1.07b Budget 2027 with record-low RM5.62m deficit
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 30 — Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow today tabled a RM1.074 billion budget for 2027, with a projected deficit of RM5.62 million.
He said the estimated deficit was the lowest in the state’s budget history, compared to the projected deficit of RM19.92 million for 2026.
The state’s estimated revenue for 2027 is RM1.069 billion, an increase of RM800,000 or 0.07 per cent compared to 2026.
The size of the 2027 operating budget is RM13.49 million, or 1.24 per cent, lower than the 2026 budget of RM1.088 billion.
“Taking into account the estimated state revenue of RM1.069 billion compared to the estimated expenditure of RM1.074 billion, Budget 2027 records the lowest estimated deficit in Penang’s budget history, at RM5.62 million,” Chow said when tabling the Supply Bill at the state legislative assembly today.
He said the budget included a contribution of RM240 million to the state development fund, compared to RM265 million in 2026.
The state has approved RM280.17 million for development expenditure in 2027, a reduction of RM38.4 million or 12.1 per cent from the previous year.
Chow said 514 development projects had been listed for implementation next year, covering public infrastructure, community facilities, sports development and strategic economic projects.
“Among the main priorities are projects to strengthen the state’s transport network and connectivity, including land acquisition for the light rail transit project, the Airport Link Road and the route to Silicon Island, as well as Phase Two of Gurney Bay and projects related to the Penang Transport Master Plan,” he said.
The chief minister said the state would continue its i-Sejahtera programme with an allocation of RM58 million for 2027.
He also announced a new Mempelai Emas programme under i-Sejahtera, offering a one-off contribution of RM500 to eligible newly married couples in Penang.
As at September 30 this year, the state had disbursed RM57.8 million through the first two phases of i-Sejahtera, benefiting 299,504 recipients, including senior citizens, persons with disabilities, single mothers and housewives.
Chow also announced that the state would maintain its 50 per cent quit rent rebate in 2027, subject to the relevant conditions.
He said quit rent collection reached RM167.59 million as at October 29, compared to RM116.05 million in 2025, an increase of RM51.54 million or 44.41 per cent.
The increase came despite the 50 per cent rebate and reductions approved through landowners’ appeals, which involved a decrease in revenue of almost RM35.7 million, he said.
On the state’s finances, Chow said revenue collection for 2025 rose to RM1.26 billion from RM810.46 million in 2024, while the state recorded a surplus of RM366.93 million compared to a deficit of RM174.09 million in 2024.
He said the balance in the consolidated revenue account rose from RM155.94 million at the end of 2024 to RM522.87 million at the end of 2025, and stood at RM651.28 million as at today.
For the period from January to October 30 this year, the state collected RM847.53 million in revenue, equivalent to 79.35 per cent of its annual estimate.
“The state government will continue to monitor revenue collection and step up follow-up action with collecting departments to ensure the 2026 revenue target of RM1.068 billion can be achieved,” he said.
Chow also announced special financial aid equivalent to one month’s salary for state civil servants.
He said a one-off payment of RM300 each would also be given to eligible religious teachers and staff, as well as teachers and staff of private Chinese schools in Penang.
The special financial aid and one-off payments, totalling RM16.207 million, will benefit 7,292 recipients and will be paid in December 2026.

Title: Cabinet agrees to amend guidelines to speed up abandoned vehicle disposal, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The Cabinet has agreed to amend the guidelines on the management of abandoned vehicles to speed up the process of removing and disposing of such vehicles, following complaints over delays and poor coordination among enforcement agencies.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the proposed amendments were put forward by the Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) and Transport Ministry (MoT) after taking into account various feedback and complaints about the existing procedures.
He said the current process could take too long and required better coordination among the agencies involved.
“The move follows various feedback and complaints about the existing guidelines and procedures for managing and disposing of abandoned vehicles, which can be lengthy and require better coordination, particularly among the agencies involved.
“The process will be taken forward by KPKT and MoT,” he told a press conference after the Cabinet meeting here today.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said today that KPKT was reviewing the need to strengthen existing legal provisions to address the issue of abandoned vehicles.
He said the proposed improvements were intended, among other things, to clarify the respective jurisdictions of the authorities and expedite enforcement and disposal procedures without compromising vehicle owners’ rights. — Bernama

Title: Govt to begin declassifying historical documents under Official Secrets Act, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The government is expected to declassify historical documents, particularly those classified as official secrets under the Official Secrets Act, as soon as possible, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim raised the matter during the second 2026 National Historians Council meeting held earlier this week.
“The Cabinet agreed with several views put forward by historians on the need to establish a general policy on the declassification of historical documents currently classified as official secrets under the Official Secrets Act.
“The prime minister expressed the view that this should be implemented as soon as possible, but carefully,” he said at his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.
Fahmi said the matter would first be examined, including by the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC), to assess its implications and determine how access to historical documents could be facilitated.
“We will consult the Attorney General’s Chambers on several aspects. We will also consult the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Home Ministry.
“However, documents that are not particularly sensitive but were previously classified under the Official Secrets Act may be easier to declassify,” he said.
Separately, Fahmi said the Cabinet had agreed to proposals by the Transport Ministry and the Housing and Local Government Ministry to amend the guidelines on the management of abandoned vehicles.
He said the move followed various feedback and complaints about the existing guidelines and disposal process, which could take too long to complete.
“There is also a need for better coordination, particularly among the relevant agencies. The process will be continued by the Housing and Local Government Ministry and the Transport Ministry,” he said.
Fahmi also said Anwar had directed the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry and the Communications Ministry, particularly through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), to take action against fraud and scams on e-commerce platforms.
“MCMC held a meeting with all major e-commerce platform operators several weeks ago.
“Meanwhile, enforcement agencies will hold a coordination meeting in the coming weeks to streamline joint action in addressing problems faced by consumers using e-commerce platforms,” he said.
Fahmi said the prime minister had instructed the relevant ministries and agencies to prioritise the matter and take immediate action.

Title: Two Penampang road upgrades worth RM173m running ahead of schedule, says Ewon
Article:
PENAMPANG, Oct 30 — Two rural road upgrade projects in Kampung Buayan and Kampung Terian here, involving a total allocation of RM173.263 million, are making positive progress, with both projects ahead of their scheduled completion timelines.
Sabah deputy chief minister III Datuk Ewon Benedick said the RM73.868 million Kampung Buayan rural road upgrade — involving a 5.6-kilometre stretch of road and the construction of two bridges — is at 76.64 per cent physical progress, 45 days ahead of schedule, and is expected to be completed in August 2027, while the RM99.395 million Kampung Terian rural road upgrade — involves a 6.7-kilometre stretch of road — is at 57.83 per cent progress, 58 days ahead of schedule, and is expected to be completed in May 2028.
“Both projects began in 2024 with funding from the Federal Government through the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW), and are monitored by the Sabah Public Works Department (JKR).
“I am satisfied with the implementation progress of these projects and hope they can be completed within the timelines set for the contractors,” the Penampang MP told reporters after visiting the project sites here today with Moyog assemblyman Datuk Donald Peter Mojuntin.
Ewon, who is also Sabah Industrial Development, Entrepreneurship and Transport Minister, said the Kampung Buayan project was progressing smoothly without requiring an extension of time (EOT), while the Kampung Terian project had been granted a one-year EOT due to land acquisition issues and the location of the concrete bridge construction.
The implementation progress of both projects had also been discussed at the Penampang District Development Action Committee meeting to ensure that their progress continued to be monitored, he added.
Meanwhile, Ewon said he and Donald would engage with relevant parties to secure funding to extend the rural road alignment to Kampung Longkogungan as part of efforts to realise the Penampang Development Master Plan 2024-2035.
He hoped that both rural road projects, together with other small-scale development projects, would improve infrastructure facilities and benefit residents and visitors to nearby villages once fully completed.
He said efforts would also be undertaken to help residents obtain land titles through the Sabah Native Customary Land Services Programme (PANTAS).
During the visit, Ewon also presented spandek roofing sheets to 33 households under the first phase of assistance to replace old roofs and agreed to allocate similar assistance to another 44 families that had submitted applications. — Bernama

Title: Deepavali: Higher Education Ministry allows online or hybrid classes from Nov 5 to 13
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) has allowed online or hybrid Teaching and Learning (PdP) sessions to be conducted at public higher education institutions from November 5 to 13 in conjunction with the Deepavali celebration on November 8.
In a statement today, MOHE said the arrangement was to enable Hindu students and teaching staff at all public universities, polytechnics and community colleges to return to their hometowns and spend time with their families during the festival.
“However, its implementation is subject to the suitability and requirements of the academic programmes at the respective institutions to ensure that teaching and learning processes run smoothly and academic activities are not disrupted,” the statement said.
It said the initiative reflected MOHE’s concern for the welfare of the higher education community, while also celebrating the cultural and religious diversity that forms the foundation of harmony in Malaysia’s multiracial society.
The ministry also extended its Deepavali greetings to all Hindu students, academic staff, ministry personnel and Malaysians.
“May this Festival of Lights bring happiness, peace and prosperity to everyone,” MOHE said. — Bernama

Title: Classic Land Rover Defender associated with Cameron Highlands to get new lease of life as tourist vehicles
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Classic Land Rover Defender vehicles associated with Cameron Highlands could continue operating as tourist vehicles despite exceeding the usual 15-year age limit under a new Transport Ministry policy.
In a statement, the ministry said the vehicles could be considered for use as Cameron Highlands Iconic Tourism Vehicles (KIPCH), provided they meet specified safety requirements, technical standards and licensing conditions.
The initiative is expected to benefit more than 60 vehicles that could potentially join the service, supporting local tourism while preserving the highland destination’s distinctive identity and heritage.
The ministry said the classic Land Rover Defenders were suited to Cameron Highlands’ hilly terrain and challenging routes, particularly for off-road tourism activities.
To ensure the policy is implemented in an orderly and controlled manner, the ministry, through the Road Transport Department (JPJ) and Land Public Transport Agency (APAD), is holding engagement sessions with stakeholders, including the Pahang state government, Cameron Highlands District Council, tourism agencies and local operators.
The discussions cover implementation arrangements such as approved routes and operating areas, designated passenger pick-up and drop-off points, licensing requirements and vehicle safety standards.
The vehicles will be restricted to tourism activities at designated locations and cannot be used to provide passenger transport services without a valid licence, the ministry said.
The ministry is targeting the rollout of the KIPCH initiative in the first quarter of 2027, subject to the finalisation of implementation arrangements, licensing requirements, safety conditions and approved operating routes.

Title: Selangor Immigration Dept repatriates 83,787 foreigners, collects RM42.6m in 17 months
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 30 — The Selangor Immigration Department (JIM) has successfully facilitated the repatriation of 83,787 foreign nationals under the Migrant Repatriation Programme (PRM) 2.0 from May 2023 to September 30.
Selangor Immigration Department acting director, Mohmad Khusairi Kamarudin, said this achievement over the 17-month period represents the highest number of registrations and applications recorded compared to other states.
“They comprise 60,913 men and 20,293 women, followed by 1,375 boys and 1,206 girls. This demonstrates the effectiveness of the initiative in addressing the issue of undocumented foreign nationals in a targeted manner.
“During the same period, the Selangor Immigration Department (JIM Selangor) also successfully collected over RM42.6 million, consisting of more than RM1.68 million in special pass fees and nearly RM41 million in compounds,” he said during a press conference at Selangor JIM headquarters here today.
In light of this, he advised foreign nationals who have violated their pass conditions or overstayed in the country to utilise the Voluntary Repatriation Programme (PRM). This can be processed at four JIM Selangor branches: Shah Alam, Port Klang, Kelana Jaya, and Kajang.
Regarding enforcement actions, Mohmad Khusairi noted that Selangor JIM continues to intensify monitoring in hotspots through the ‘Mega Integrated Enforcement Operation,’ which is being conducted on an ongoing basis.
In the latest operation which began at 10 pm last night and concluded early this morning, 321 individuals were screened during targeted raids across the Shah Alam, Subang Jaya, and Klang areas.
“The premises raided included an entertainment centre (KTV), two factories, one processing plastic goods and the other manufacturing boxes as well as five blocks of flats housing foreign nationals. The operation involved 130 personnel, comprising 115 officers from JIM Selangor, along with representatives from the Employees Provident Fund (7), the Department of Labour (4), and the Malaysia Civil Defence Force (4).”
“Further checks revealed that 242 foreign nationals, aged between 25 and 50, were detained for various immigration offenses — including the lack of identification documents, violation of pass conditions, and overstaying,” he said.
He said those arrested comprised 180 men and 62 women from Bangladesh (57), India (58), Indonesia (44), Myanmar (52), Vietnam (16), Thailand (4), Nepal (4), Pakistan (2), Laos (2), as well as refugees from Myanmar (2) and Cambodia (1).
He added that all detainees have been placed at the Semenyih Immigration Depot for further action. Meanwhile, five ‘Form 29’ notices (summonses for witnesses) were issued to Malaysian nationals suspected to be employers to assist with the investigation.
Addressing the presence of foreign nationals featured on the accounts of social media influencers, Mohmad Khusairi noted that his department has a dedicated social media team to monitor such content and he also encouraged the public to come forward with complaints or information.
“Many locations that were raided previously have been found to be operational again, and we require the public’s cooperation in providing information,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian man, Vietnamese wife get 30 years for 173kg meth trafficking
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The High Court today sentenced a couple to 30 years in prison after finding them guilty of trafficking 173kg of methamphetamine four years ago.
Judge Nurulhuda Nur’aini Mohamad Nor handed down the sentence on Adam Tan Seng Tek, 34, and Vietnamese national Nguyen Thi Kim Thanh, 33, after finding that the defence had failed to raise reasonable doubt at the close of the defence case.
“The court finds that the prosecution has successfully proven its case beyond reasonable doubt and finds both accused guilty and convicted on the charge,” she said.
The court ordered the prison sentence to run from the couple’s arrest on Feb 24, 2022, with Tan also receiving 12 strokes of the cane.
According to the charge, they were accused of jointly trafficking 172,741.10g of methamphetamine at a condominium unit at Residensi Kiara Jalil 1 here at 9.30pm on February 24, 2022.
They were charged under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which provides for the death penalty or life imprisonment and not fewer than 12 strokes of the cane, if not sentenced to death.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Goh Ai Rene sought a heavy sentence, citing the quantity of drugs involved at 172.74kg.
“In this case, I urge the court to take into account the weight of the drugs involved as well as public interest, apart from the fact that the second accused (Nguyen) is a foreign national who committed the offence in this country.
“Drug offences pose a threat to national security, public order and public health. Drugs were also declared the country’s number one enemy in 1983,” she said.
Lawyer Kee Wei Loon, representing both accused, sought life imprisonment for his clients, citing the sentencing trend in such cases where courts no longer impose the death penalty and instead opt for life imprisonment. — Bernama

Title: Domestic helper who punched autistic boy 23 times, recorded abuse jailed in Singapore
Article:
SINGAPORE, Oct 30 — A 29-year-old Indonesian domestic helper has reportedly been sentenced to three years in jail for abusing a four-year-old autistic boy in her care, including punching him at least 23 times despite his attempts to protect himself.
According to Singapore’s
CNA
, the woman, whose identity cannot be disclosed to protect the victims, also kicked the boy’s head twice in a separate incident and recorded videos of her employer’s children naked.
The court reportedly heard that the boy was non-verbal and unable to alert his parents to the abuse, making him particularly vulnerable.
The woman, who began working for the family in January, also allegedly sprayed water directly into the face of the family’s one-year-old boy using a handheld shower head for 16 seconds, causing him to flinch and cry.
The abuse reportedly came to light in March when her employer discovered videos and photographs of the incidents, along with images of his naked children, on her phone.
Investigations subsequently uncovered four videos and two photographs showing the children naked in the toilet, with the woman having sent two videos and both photographs to her husband,
CNA
reported.
Prosecutors reportedly said the woman had acted out of exhaustion and frustration from caring for the autistic boy, but stressed that her circumstances did not justify the violence.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohamed Riasudeen sought between 35 and 41 months’ imprisonment, while defence lawyer Ariffin Sha argued for a sentence of two years and 10-and-a-half months, noting that she had apologised and previously requested a transfer from the household.
Both sides reportedly agreed that the recordings of the naked children were not made for sexual gratification, although prosecutors argued that her position as their caregiver aggravated the offences.
In sentencing her, District Judge Sharmila Sripathy-Shanaz emphasised the serious breach of trust involved in abusing a child who could neither speak for himself nor seek help.
“Stress is not a license for violence nor is frustration an excuse for cruelty,” the judge said, adding that the sentence would have been considerably longer had there been evidence of physical injury.

Title: Home Ministry: Refugee registration card not a path to Malaysian citizenship, PR or permanent stay
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The Home Ministry (KDN) has stressed that the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) Programme is not a pathway for refugees to remain in Malaysia permanently, obtain Permanent Resident (PR) status or acquire Malaysian citizenship.
KDN said any employment access granted to DPP holders is temporary and limited, and subject to conditions and government approval.
“DPP is also not an incentive or pull factor for new refugees to enter Malaysia. The government has set January 1, 2023 as the eligibility cut-off date, meaning only individuals who were already in Malaysia before that date may be considered for participation in the programme,” it said in a statement today.
KDN said possession of a card or letter issued by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) does not automatically confer eligibility.
It said the government will continue to repatriate refugees to their countries of origin and resettle them in third countries and that the implementation of the DPP does not change that objective.
“Instead, the DPP is a mechanism to identify, screen, document and monitor existing refugees while a final solution is implemented in accordance with the law,” it said.
KDN also clarified that granting employment access to DPP holders does not mean the country’s labour market is being opened up freely to refugees.
According to KDN, the implementation takes into account the actual needs of industries, particularly sectors that continue to face labour shortages for 3D (dirty, dangerous and difficult) jobs that are less likely to be taken up by local workers.
“Priority for employment opportunities for Malaysian citizens remains protected, in line with the foreign worker employment policy and national security interests,” it said.
At the same time, KDN said lawful employment access would enable refugees to acquire skills, experience and verifiable employment records.
“This can help them meet the criteria for alternative resettlement pathways to third countries, including employment mobility programmes offered by host countries,” it said.
KDN explained that the approach would also enable the government to manage foreign workers who are already in Malaysia in a controlled manner, thereby reducing the need to bring in new foreign workers to fill certain vacancies.
It said the refugee issue was a legacy problem that had persisted for decades and posed major challenges to the country in terms of the economy, society, security and law enforcement.
Therefore, KDN, together with the Foreign Ministry, will continue efforts to cooperate with countries of origin and third countries to facilitate long-term solutions. — Bernama

Title: Cabinet approves UUCA amendments to lift curbs on students’ freedom, new law planned
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The Cabinet today approved proposals to amend the existing Universities and University Colleges Act (UUCA), particularly provisions seen as restricting students’ freedom of expression and association, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said the Cabinet also agreed to develop a new law that would eventually replace the UUCA entirely within a reasonable timeframe.
“The Cabinet today approved a proposal by the Higher Education Ministry to undertake two measures concerning the Universities and University Colleges Act (UUCA).
“The first is to amend the existing Act, particularly sections viewed as restricting students’ freedom of expression and association.
“The second is to develop a new law that will eventually replace the UUCA entirely within a reasonable timeframe,” he said at his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.
Fahmi said the Cabinet had also agreed for the Higher Education Minister to table amendments to the existing UUCA in Parliament this December.
“The amendments will specifically address provisions that restrict students’ freedom.
“In December, God-willing, the Higher Education Minister will table amendments to the existing UUCA,” he said.
He said the proposed amendments were intended to immediately remove provisions that restrict students’ freedom.
However, Fahmi said drafting a new law to fully replace the existing Act would take more time, particularly as it would cover matters such as university registration, listing, management and other related aspects.
“This is because the Higher Education Ministry needs to consider several new aspects of university administration.
“We expect this to happen in 2027, although no specific year or timeline has been formally determined during the meeting. But we are looking at next year,” he added.

Title: Nadma advises public against panic buying ahead of north-east monsoon
Article:
PUCHONG, Oct 30 — The public has been advised against panic buying or excessively stockpiling food amid concerns over the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL), and instead to make preparations according to their respective needs.
National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said the spread of unverified information, particularly on social media, could trigger panic buying, potentially leading to other problems, including disruptions to the supply of goods.
“I have seen posts on Facebook, where friends are suggesting to stock up on food. We should avoid such panic-buying messages.
“Sometimes, panic buying creates another problem, not a Northeast Monsoon disaster, but a shortage of goods instead. Just buy according to your needs,” he said after the media engagement session on the government’s preparedness for the MTL here today.
Meor Ismail said the public should take basic precautionary measures, including keeping important documents and belongings in elevated places to prevent them from being damaged in the event of floods.
He also advised families with elderly members, persons with disabilities (PwD) and pregnant women to plan their evacuation to safer locations in advance if their residential areas are at risk of flooding.
He said the public should also stay informed of weather updates and forecasts from official sources and move to temporary relief centres immediately when instructed to do so.
Meor Ismail said temporary relief centres have been prepared to ensure that the welfare of flood victims can be properly taken care of.
At the same time, he reminded all parties, particularly social media influencers, against creating sensational content that could cause public anxiety to gain followers.
“Do not spread sensational news, including influencers. In the past, we have had to arrest people who posted videos that could cause panic,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Govt, parties to jointly monitor reform commitments under Bersatu CSA, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The development allocations provided for reforms under the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) will be monitored jointly by the government and the parties that signed the agreement, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said the monitoring would follow a mechanism established under the previous CSA, which involved joint assessments by both parties to determine whether the agreed commitments had been fulfilled.
“We believe this could be one way of implementing the monitoring process, similar to what we witnessed previously.
“The government intends to fulfil the commitments made under this CSA, particularly those involving institutional reforms.
“We hope that, with the strong support received, we will be able to implement these reforms,” he said at his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.
Yesterday, Bersatu signed the CSA in Parliament, pledging its support for the Supply Bill 2027, or Budget 2027.
Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin told reporters that, in return, the government had agreed to provide the party’s MPs with the same constituency development allocations given to government MPs.
He said the agreement also covered institutional reforms, including proposals to limit the prime minister’s tenure to two terms and separate the powers of the Attorney General.
Muhyiddin stressed that Bersatu would remain in the Opposition and continue to provide checks and balances.
Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman was also among those involved in the signing, which was facilitated by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.
Fahmi described the latest CSA signing as a positive development for the country’s political stability, saying it reflected a spirit of cooperation in implementing various institutional reform initiatives.
He also clarified that the signing of the memorandum of understanding (MoU), or CSA, was not limited to the 13 MPs involved.
He said the agreement remained open to any other MP who wished to come forward for discussions and sign it.
“Therefore, the door for further discussions remains open,” he said.

Title: Melaka polls: Fire Dept conducts safety checks at nomination, vote-tallying centres
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 30 — The Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) has inspected 28 nomination and official vote-tallying centres ahead of the 16th Melaka state election.
Melaka JBPM director Mohd Zaidi Ma’at said the inspections were conducted at the request of the Election Commission (EC) to ensure that fire safety facilities at the centres were in good working order.
“The inspections cover fire safety systems and emergency exits to ensure that safety at nomination and polling centres is given due attention.
“So far, all centres inspected have met fire safety requirements, and we are prepared to respond to any emergencies throughout the election process,” he told Bernama after the Melaka JBPM monthly assembly at the department’s state headquarters in Bukit Katil here today.
Mohd Zaidi said the department had earlier conducted joint simulation exercises with the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the EC in Masjid Tanah to prepare for possible incidents, including riots, fires and other emergencies.
“The exercises aim to ensure that the agencies involved are prepared to coordinate their response in the event of an incident requiring assistance from JBPM,” he said.
Mohd Zaidi added that all fire stations in Melaka had been placed on standby to respond to potential emergencies, including fires and floods, throughout the state election.
The EC has set November 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka state election, with nomination day tomorrow and early voting on November 10. — Bernama

Title: Two charged with posting extremely offensive comments against Tuanku Muhriz on social media
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Two men pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to charges of creating and posting extremely offensive comments against Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, on social media in August.
The accused, unemployed Abdullah Aidid Mochtar @ Ahmad Duta, 44, and graphic designer Ashadi Zul’izzi Zainal Abidin, 46, entered the plea after the charges were read before Judge Muhammad Ilmami Ahmad.
Abdullah Aidid is accused of creating and initiating the transmission of extremely offensive communications with intent to offend through the TikTok account “rookiebenz_albenzauto” at 11.27pm on August 1, while Ashadi Zul’izzi is accused of the same act via the Threads account “razakahmad725” at 2.39pm on August 4.
The posts were viewed at Jalan Dutamas Seroja 5, Taman Segambut (SPPK) here at 12.34pm on August 4 and 12.15pm on August 5, respectively.
Both were charged under Section 233(1)(a) of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 and face punishment under Section 233(2) of the same Act.
If convicted, they face a maximum fine of RM500,000 or up to two years’ jail, or both, plus a further fine of RM5,000 for each day the offence persists after conviction.
Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) prosecuting officer Nazrul Nizam Mohd Zameri offered bail of RM15,000 with one surety for each accused, citing the nature of the charges involving extremely offensive communications against the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.
Abdullah Aidid, who was unrepresented, appealed for lower bail on the grounds that he had lost his job following the case and has been unemployed for the past three months.
Ashadi Zul’izzi, also unrepresented, sought lower bail as the amount offered by the prosecution was beyond his means.
The court then allowed each accused bail of RM12,000 with one surety and fixed December 1 for mention. — Bernama

Title: Kluang council shuts down LED screens after obscene video appears in suspected hack
Article:
KLUANG, Oct 30 — The Kluang Municipal Council (MPK) will investigate an incident where its public message LED display system in several locations were hacked, resulting in displaying an obscene video last night.
The municipal council said it has since lodged a police report to facilitate further investigation into the embarrassing incident.
“A comprehensive investigation is being undertaken in collaboration with the screen’s vendor to identify the main cause of the incident.
“This is in addition to implementing remedial measures and strengthening the system's security,” said a brief statement issued today.
MPK also apologised for any inconvenience caused to the Kluang community following the incident.
Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said he had received a report regarding the incident.
“For your information, the MPK's LED system was hacked and the council has taken proactive measures by shutting down all LED screens under its jurisdiction,” he said briefly when contacted by the media today.
Earlier, the offensive incident was captured on a Facebook reel that have since been taken down.
The video also contained a watermark that credited the Leakers.Gov cyber hacking group.
In the short video, the public were taken aback where the LED screen displayed the obscene images. This later sparked concern among the public.
It is understood that there were other reports of similar embarrassing incidents involving MPK’s LED screens, including Dataran Tasik Kluang, Taman Intan and the area along the route towards Kahang.

Title: Malaysia takes delivery of first two South Korean FA-50M fighter jets
Article:
LABUAN, Oct 30 — Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin today received the first two FA-50M light combat aircraft acquired by the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), marking an important milestone in the country’s efforts to strengthen its air defence capabilities.
The two aircraft, developed by Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI), arrived today at RMAF Labuan base, after being flown from Sacheon, Republic of Korea.
“The official handover ceremony is scheduled to take place in mid-November at RMAF Kuantan Air Base,” he told reporters at RMAF Labuan base here today.
Khaled described the acquisition as a significant moment for the country in enhancing its military capabilities and safeguarding national sovereignty.
He said the acquisition also supported the RMAF’s long-term capability development under its Capability Development Plan 2055, commonly known as CAP55.
He said the government would also consider acquiring a second batch of more modern and advanced fighter aircraft to further strengthen the country’s air defence capabilities, although the country of origin for future procurement had yet to be determined.
“The 18 FA-50M aircraft were procured under Malaysia’s Fighter Lead-In Training and Light Combat Aircraft programme, following the planned decommissioning of the RMAF’s Hawk aircraft in 2028,” he said.
Khaled said RMAF was expected to receive a total of six FA-50M aircraft by April 2027, with the remaining units scheduled for delivery in early 2028.
He said the ministry would determine the number of FA-50M aircraft to be based in Labuan following the decommissioning of the Hawk aircraft.
The FA-50M is a two-seat aircraft capable of supporting crewed flight training as well as demanding operational missions.
It can reach speeds of up to Mach 1.2, enabling it to fly faster than the speed of sound and operate at high altitudes.
Meanwhile, 57 core personnel comprising six pilots, six engineering officers and 45 technicians have completed their training in the Republic of Korea to spearhead the new squadron.
All six pilots in the initial training group completed their flight training programme on Oct 21.
Mohamed Khaled said the aircraft would be operated by No. 15 Squadron, which already has more than 200 personnel, with preparations for its home base centred at the RMAF Kuantan Air Base. — Bernama

Title: Puchong halal raid nets 6.5 tonnes of chicken allegedly scalded before slaughter, 12 foreign workers held
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — More than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken suspected of being processed without complying with Islamic slaughtering requirements and halal certification standards were seized during a raid on a warehouse in Puchong here shortly after midnight yesterday.
Twelve Bangladeshi and Pakistani men, believed to be involved in slaughtering and processing chickens at the premises, were also detained during the operation, codenamed Op Taring Chiller.
Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA) Wildlife Crime Control Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence (WCB/PSK) commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said the raid, conducted at 12.40am, uncovered premises suspected of being used to slaughter, process and distribute fresh chicken without valid halal certification.
He said preliminary inspections revealed slaughtering and handling practices that raised serious concerns over compliance with Islamic requirements and the halal status of the products.
“Inspections found that the chickens were believed to have been immersed in hot water until they died before being slaughtered,” he said in a statement today.
The integrated operation was carried out in collaboration with the Selangor Islamic Religious Department, Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim), Department of Environment and Petaling District Health Office.
Mohd Zaki said authorities seized 468 plastic packages containing raw chicken weighing approximately 6,555 kilogrammes, with an estimated value of RM85,400.
Preliminary investigations indicated that the premises had allegedly been operating as a chicken slaughtering, processing and distribution centre for some time, with supplies sourced from several poultry farms around Sepang.
“The processed chicken was believed to have been distributed to customers, including restaurants, grocery shops and supermarkets across the Klang Valley,” he said.
The case is being investigated under Sections 3(1)(a) and 4(1) of the Trade Descriptions (Definition of Halal) Order 2011 and Section 38(1) of the Environmental Quality Act 1974.
The 12 foreign nationals are also being investigated under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 and Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963. — Bernama

Title: Adat Perpatih must be preserved and documented for future generations, says N. Sembilan MB
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 30 — Adat Perpatih, a matrilineal customary law system practised predominantly in Negeri Sembilan, must be preserved and documented through digital technology, academic publications and heritage education to ensure the state’s cultural traditions are not lost over time.
Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said safeguarding the heritage was not solely the responsibility of customary institutions and museums, but required the involvement of communities, educational institutions and government agencies.
“Knowledge of the customs, oral histories and traditional practices must be documented for future generations and made more accessible through interactive exhibitions to help the public better understand this heritage.
“Adat Perpatih is more than a set of inherited customs. It embodies a philosophy of life that emphasises consensus, consultation, justice and shared responsibility,” he said when officiating Perpatih Fest 2026, themed Adat Dijaga, Warisan Terpelihara here today.
Ismail said customary leaders, educational institutions and government agencies had an important role in ensuring traditional knowledge and practices were passed down to future generations.
Meanwhile, the menteri besar said Adat Perpatih and the cultural traditions of other communities also had the potential to contribute to the state’s economy through traditional cuisine, performing arts, handicrafts and local history as tourism attractions.
In conjunction with Visit Negeri Sembilan Year 2026, the state government aims to strengthen cultural heritage as a tourism product that attracts visitors while creating economic opportunities for local entrepreneurs.
Ismail said this year’s Perpatih Fest also featured a delegation from Thailand interested in learning more about Adat Perpatih, providing an opportunity to introduce the tradition to a wider international audience.
The three-day Perpatih Fest, running from today until November 1, features demonstrations of traditional luak customs, traditional games, museum and ethnic exhibitions, heritage cuisine and cultural performances.
The festival also includes seminars, discussions and forums on customary institutions and the cultural history of the Malay Archipelago, alongside traditional costume competitions and creative activities aimed at bringing cultural heritage closer to younger generations. — Bernama
